records.article:
# Do the onion cookies reveal text by XOR?

The [H‑03 source test](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round16/zeroFP) takes two 32-byte values from the 2013 onion cookies and XORs each with eight successive 32-byte blocks of four objects: the LP2-49–51 grid payload and three later onion RSA-hex blobs. We replayed its executable with the exact preserved inputs and independently recomputed every output byte.

![For each cookie and object, the most printable of eight XOR blocks remains below the 26-of-32-byte gate.](experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/xor-maxima.svg)

**None of the 64 executed blocks reaches the source's 80% printable-ASCII gate.** The highest has **20 of 32** printable bytes, from cookie 761 with the fourth object. A deliberately planted 32-byte ASCII block is recovered by the original source function, so this threshold can detect that kind of output. The [complete 64-case table](experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/cases.json) preserves the XOR bytes and counts.

## What the null covers

The source's written plan describes **128 trials** using both raw and hex-decoded cookie forms, plus digest and PKCS-structure checks. Its saved executable performs **64 trials using the hex-decoded form**. It applies the printable gate and records only a two-byte `00 01` hint; it does not execute the full written digest or padding tests. Our replay matches the executable and saved result, so the negative applies to **these 64 block-aligned XOR operations**, not to every use of the cookies as keys or the full written plan.

The remaining raw-form cases cannot be reproduced as written: each file contains **64 ASCII hex characters**, while the plan pairs a “32-byte cookie” with each **32-byte block** and never says which 32 raw characters to use or whether to repeat, truncate or change block size. We did not invent that rule. The plan also leaves the set and encoding of “known 3301 hashes/strings” unspecified.

A [separately frozen, retrospective diagnostic](experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/structure-plan.json) checks the same 64 outputs for the source code's PKCS helper pattern, a stricter eight-`FF` padding pattern, and the one **20-byte AN END prefix** explicitly named in that code. All three yield **zero matches**; synthetic examples pass each predicate. This only addresses those exact structures in the executed 64 outputs. The helper accepts one `FF`, so its rule is not a general statement that a block is valid PKCS#1 padding.

The objects are exact local source bytes, including `canon_256.bin`; a different grid transcription would be a different input. No readable plaintext or new key is recovered here.

## Reproduce

The [replay plan](experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/replay-plan.json) hashes the pinned source programs and six input files. Run from the repository root with Python:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/run.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/structure.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-h03-onion-cookie-xor/plot.py
```

The first command runs the original H‑03 function and a temporary planted case. The second recomputes all 64 XORs without importing that function and compares the source's saved summary. This plan was frozen before our replay, **after** the source's result was available; it is not a new preregistration.

record_type.label: Source or input audit
record_type.description: Checks image provenance, extraction or input coverage against a declared reference; it does not establish a decryption.

scope.representation: The 56 LP2-00–55 hosted JPEGs whose exact bytes match the pinned source capsule, the four original source scripts, the source canon and archived reports.
scope.procedure: Hash-check all source files and images; run unmodified segmentation, template clustering, template-DP reading and count alignment in an isolated temporary tree; compare fresh and archived summaries. The independent checker redoes both length alignments from compact receipts.

records.finding: Both runs have 646 line bands and 13,140 full-height glyphs. Four of 646 band glyph counts differ, leaving the fresh read with 16,237 glyphs versus 16,245 archived. The historical 226 classes are a saved output, not a source-code gate. The fresh 95.83% rune-label fit uses zero held-out lines.

The source's class-to-rune mapping is trained and scored on the same canonical LP2 lines, so its agreement is not independent transcription accuracy. records.article:
## Finding

**The image-reading pipeline runs on all 56 original LP2 JPEGs, but its saved output does not reproduce exactly.** The fresh run finds the same **646 line bands** and **13,140 full-height glyphs** as the archived run. It groups the glyphs into **229 shapes**, compared with **226** archived, and finds **233 lines** whose rune count matches the reference text, compared with **232** archived.

![The fresh image read and archived run agree on line bands, but differ slightly in shape classes and count-matching lines.](experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/pipeline.svg)

Only **4 of 646** line-band glyph counts changed: one on LP2-08, two on LP2-22, and one on LP2-54. The fresh run reads eight fewer glyphs in total. The 226-class figure is a saved result, not a required check in the code; the reader accepts every shape class seen at least 100 times. Its fresh 229-class bank selects 33 templates, while the archived bank selected 32. A fresh run can therefore be used as a **new, explicitly pinned instrument**, but it must not be presented as the original archived array or as proof that the reference transcription is correct.

## What the stages establish

The original programs first locate line bands, collect glyph images, group similar shapes, and then choose a low-cost sequence of those shapes for each line. Those stages do **not** read the canonical rune transcription. We used the [pinned source code](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/retranscribe) without changing its rules and checked every hosted image against the source's byte hashes.

The final program compares the image-derived sequences with the LP2 reference text. It first aligns lines by length. The **233 count-matching lines** are a useful check on segmentation, but a matching length alone does not prove that the runes match. The program then learns a mapping from shape classes to rune letters **using those same lines** and reports **95.83% agreement on them**. It uses **zero held-out lines** and does not train on solved LP1 pages. This percentage is an in-sample fit, not an independent transcription accuracy estimate.

We do not know why the fresh and archived shape counts differ. A single-thread run and a stable-sort diagnostic still produced 229 classes. The original archived NPZ arrays have no available hashes, so their contents cannot be compared byte for byte. This record does not settle any disputed rune or test a cipher.

## Reproduce

The [plan](experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/plan.json) pins the 56 image hashes, original code, canonical text and historical reports. The [results](experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/results.json) hold the fresh artifact hashes; [line counts](experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/line-counts.json) allow a separate checker to redo both count-based alignments without using the source program.

The compact check takes seconds from a Liberpedia checkout:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/check.py
```

For the full image rebuild, use Python with NumPy, SciPy and Pillow, and a checkout of the [pinned source revision](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1). The wrapper verifies all source and image hashes, copies them into a temporary directory, then runs the four original programs in order. This takes several minutes and does not overwrite the saved results:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/run.py --source-root PATH/TO/liber-primus --site-root . --rebuild --check
```

The checker verifies the compact receipts and, when given source and artifact directories, their bytes. It does **not** classify image pixels independently. Any follow-on test using these new arrays must identify them by their hashes rather than silently inherit the archived 226-class result.

records.article:
# Do the lines carry another message?

This [published test](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round19/C3/l3) measures the line layout in the 56 unsolved LP2 page images. It asks whether line height, margins, spacing, or rune counts form a second data channel. We ran its two programs on the **exact 56 JPEGs** used by the source and reproduced their saved results: every count and verdict matches; eleven floating-point values differ by less than 10⁻¹².

## What did the search find?

The source measured **616 image rows**. Five of eleven measured features split into two groups under its mixture-model rule. That is a property of the layout, **not a decoded message**. Its eight specified bit-decoding searches found no qualifying English four-gram pattern.

One correlation also crossed the source's multiple-test threshold: lines with more runes tended to have lower mean rune indices (*ρ* = −0.257). A width-adjusted calculation fell to *ρ* = −0.018. This suggests a typographic explanation, but the source pairs image rows and canonical text lines by position even though there are **616 versus 604**; that alignment needs checking before interpreting the cross-domain relationship. The rune-count/rune-index correlation itself uses the canonical lines.

## Did the decoder pass its own controls?

![The strongest planted line-fill signal recovered 85.9% of bits, below the required 95%; a separate ASCII plant matched 29 of 77 intended characters despite a source PASS label.](experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/control-gates.svg)

The source required **95% recovery** of a planted 64-bit message to establish sensitivity. Its strongest line-fill plant recovered **55 of 64 bits (85.9%)**; none of seven tested strengths passed. In a separate noise-free ASCII plant, the source marked a four-gram score as “PASS.” We reconstructed the actual decoded text: only **29 of 77 characters** match the planted text. A favorable score did not mean the message was recovered.

The eight negative bit scans therefore describe **this decoder on these channels**. They cannot exclude a line-based message that this procedure lacks the power to recover. Nor do the measured layout groups by themselves establish such a message.

## Reproduce

The [frozen replay plan](experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/source-replay-plan.json) pins source files, rules, and image hashes. Extract the [original images](downloads/original-images.zip) into `images/`, or use a complete Liberpedia checkout. The experiment ZIP includes the pinned MIT-licensed source subset. From the repository root, with Python, NumPy, SciPy, and Pillow:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/run.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/check.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/plot.py --check
```

The [source geometry rows](experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/source-linegeom.json), [source tests](experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/source-linetests.json), [summary](experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/results.json), and [independent control recount](experiments/records/dukotah-line-geometry-channel-replay/independent-controls.json) are included. The plan was frozen before our replay, **after** the source findings were known; this is a source check, not an independent preregistration.

records.title: Long-key search with optional skipped positions
records.question: Does a pinned beam search over three long candidate keys recover complete text from six unsolved LP2 pages?
records.summary: The archived 54-case beam search reproduces and finds no score above its −5 bar. In 18 planted collision-skip cases with the correct key, all scores clear that bar but none recover the exact text, so the source screen cannot exclude the proposed mechanism.

record_type.label: Method replay
record_type.description: Reconstructs a supplied proposed method and its choices; reproduction is not independent confirmation of a reading.

scope.representation: Pinned krisyotam rune-only source segments, which agree exactly with site rune sequences. The rune-free LP2-50 segment is omitted; tested source indices are identical to listed site page IDs.
scope.procedure: Execute unmodified Campaign VII C1 source in a temporary copy, then reconstruct its 120-state beam independently for all 54 full-page settings. Plant two known-text lengths with and without collision-triggered key skips across every source key and offset, checking complete plaintext equality separately from the source score bar.
scope.parameters: Three named source key texts × six longest source unsolved pages × offsets 0, floor(length/4), floor(length/2) = 54 searches. Beam width120; steps 1 or2 permitted unconditionally. 36 planted control decodes (3 texts × 3 offsets × 2 lengths × 2 mechanisms).
scope.exclusions: No other key texts, all offsets, other pages, alternate scorer or beam width, or skip restriction tied to ciphertext doublets. No pagewise shuffle significance test after the collision-skip positive failed exact recovery.

records.finding: Best manuscript score: −6.086 on LP2-17; 0/54 exceed −5. All 18 planted collision-skip cases exceed −5 but 0/18 reproduce the full known plaintext. An additional 18 no-skip plants score above the bar and 11/18 recover exact text. Independent reconstruction confirms all source outputs are full-length.
records.limitations: The executable beam permits a one- or two-position key advance at every rune without enforcing a would-be doublet collision. The fixed English score can prefer incorrect paths. The three texts, three coarse offsets, six longest pages and beam width120 do not represent all long keys or decoders. Repeated known text is a synthetic detector check.
records.article:
# A long running key with skipped positions

A pinned Campaign VII program tried three candidate books or prose texts as long keys. At every manuscript rune, its decoder searched paths that advance **one or two key positions**, keeping the 120 paths it scored highest. The source tested 54 page/key/offset combinations; none reached its −5 English-score bar. We reproduce its best score, **−6.086 on LP2-17**, and all 54 complete outputs.

The decisive qualification is the decoder's **known-message test**. We encrypted documented text with the same key texts and a rule that skips a key position only when the ordinary draw would repeat the previous ciphertext rune. All **18** planted skip cases passed the source's English-score bar, yet **zero recovered the complete original text**. The score can therefore say “English-like” about a *different* path. The archived no-hit result is a bounded search result, not an exclusion of this cipher mechanism.

![A comparison shows all 18 planted collision-skip cases pass the score bar but none recover exact plaintext; all 54 manuscript searches stay below the bar.](experiments/records/dukotah-longkey-skip-beam/comparison.svg)

| Input to the same decoder | Above source score bar | Complete exact reading |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Known text, ordinary key advance | 18/18 | 11/18 |
| Known text, collision-triggered skips | 18/18 | **0/18** |
| Unsolved LP2 pages | 0/54 | Unknown |

The first collision-skip control in the fixed test order uses the Tao Te Ching key at offset zero, the 85-rune known reading, and two planted skips. It returns a *higher* English score than the known text (−4.335 versus −4.462), but its **19th rune** is `TH` where the known text has `B`:

```text
Known     ...INTHEDEEPWE|BTHEREEXISTSAP...
Returned  ...INTHEDEEPWE|THTHEREEXISTSAP...
```

These are continuous rune transliterations, with no added word spaces. The vertical bar marks the first differing rune boundary; the dots mark omitted runes. Both readings clear the source's −5 bar, so that bar alone cannot tell the correct path from the wrong one.

The controls use the 85-rune documented `AN END` reading and a deterministic 273-rune repetition of it, at each of the three source offsets for each of the three keys. The longer sample is close to the tested page lengths of 273–277 runes. Repetition makes it a detector check, not a second independent natural passage. Several planted paths without a collision-triggered skip also lose the correct text because the beam is allowed to choose a higher-scoring path.

## What the source actually searches

The fixed key texts are a Tao Te Ching file, a Gospel of Thomas file, and Cicada PGP prose from the pinned repository. The source selects the six longest rune-bearing unsolved segments: LP2-29, 43, 47, 11, 17 and 21. Each key is tried at its beginning, one-quarter point and halfway point. That is **3 texts × 6 pages × 3 offsets = 54 searches**. The source's saved top result and our complete output ledger agree.

The source description calls this a *doublet-avoiding* running-key search. Its executable beam, however, permits either advance at **every** rune; it does **not** check whether the extra advance would prevent a doublet. We replay the executable rule exactly and use collision-triggered encryption only for the planted control. That distinction is why this result cannot be generalized to a decoder that enforces the collision condition.

The English score ranks transliterated rune output by a pinned four-letter frequency model. It is a useful search heuristic, but choosing the best of many beam paths can give a convincing score to an incorrect reconstruction. The planted control measures that failure directly. Other keys, starting points, pages, beam widths, and a collision-constrained decoder are outside the test.

## Reproduce

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/dukotah-longkey-skip-beam/plan.json) pins all three key files, the source grid and control construction. [Results](experiments/records/dukotah-longkey-skip-beam/results.json) include every manuscript score and all 36 planted cases. Run from a Liberpedia checkout:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-longkey-skip-beam/run.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-longkey-skip-beam/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-longkey-skip-beam/plot.py --check
```

The runner executes the [unmodified source program](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/corpus/H-branch-recovery/recovered/claude_master-roadmap-libra-qk527u/liber-primus/analysis/campaign7/c1_skipkey.py) in a temporary copy and matches its saved result. The independent checker reconstructs the beam, all 54 outputs, all 36 plants and the source-to-site rune mapping. The source program and exact key files are bundled with their hashes. Its archived report predates our planted controls; the control findings are new to this replay.

records.title: Does LP2's rune order reveal a generator?
records.question: Does a published first-order entropy dip survive a control that matches the manuscript's scarce adjacent repeats?
records.summary: The published 40-control entropy anomaly reproduces exactly, but it lies inside a new 1,000-stream control range after matching LP2's 86 adjacent repeats.

record_type.label: Manuscript measurement
record_type.description: Measures a stated feature or statistical comparison; it does not test a complete decoding rule.

scope.representation: Pinned source GP29 transcription, 55 concatenated nonempty LP2 text segments, 12,956 runes; includes cross-segment transitions.
scope.procedure: Replay unchanged 40-iid-control source program exactly. Separately, compare empirical order-zero through order-two conditional entropy to 1,000 seeded controls constructed with exactly 86 adjacent repeat transitions.
scope.parameters: 29 symbols, 12,956 runes, source 40 iid controls seed 3301; new matched controls seed 20261023, 1,000 replicates, 86 repeated transitions each.
scope.exclusions: No pagewise or wordwise matching, exact unigram-count conditioning, held-out predictive entropy, PPM, key search, or decryption.

records.finding: Published order-one entropy is 4.7854 versus 4.8125 for 40 independent controls (z -14.6). Among 1,000 post-observation controls with exactly 86 adjacent repeats, the mean is 4.7871 and 207 are at or below LP2. The prominent dip is not exceptional under that matched model.
records.limitations: The new controls were chosen after the anomaly and match only total adjacent repeats, not page structure, exact unigram counts, or word boundaries. In-sample high-order empirical entropy is not a held-out entropy-rate estimate; no key or plaintext is identified.
records.article:
# Is LP2's rune order unusually predictable?

A [published analysis](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/recon/i6_mdl) compared 12,956 unsolved LP2 runes with 40 uniformly random streams. Its strongest result was a lower first-order conditional entropy: **4.7854** versus **4.8125** bits per rune, reported as *z* = −14.6. We reproduced every numeric field by running the unchanged source code.

## What changes when repeats are matched?

![The LP2 first-order entropy is far below independent random controls, but inside the range of controls constructed with the same number of adjacent repeats.](experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/order-one-controls.svg)

LP2 has only **86 adjacent equal-rune pairs** in 12,955 transitions. An independently random stream has many more. An ordinary first-order entropy calculation sees this missing transition and can look unusually low without identifying a cipher rule.

We therefore made 1,000 new control streams with **exactly 86** adjacent repeats each. Their mean first-order entropy is **4.7871**, and their middle 95% spans **4.7826–4.7915**. LP2's **4.7854** falls inside; **207 of 1,000** controls are at or below it. Under this specific repeat-matched model, the prominent first-order dip is no longer exceptional.

| Entropy order | LP2 | Repeat-matched mean | LP2 position among 1,000 controls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No previous rune | 4.8565 | 4.8565 | 480 at or below |
| One previous rune | 4.7854 | 4.7871 | 207 at or below |
| Two previous runes | 3.5228 | 3.5196 | 685 at or below |

The source also tried compressors and phrase counts; their outputs replay exactly. Its order-three through order-five empirical entropies become very small for both LP2 and random controls because nearly all long contexts are seen too few times. Those in-sample values do **not** estimate a held-out entropy rate or establish that the text is generated by a PRNG, a hash chain, or a one-time pad.

## What this covers

The source joins its **55 nonempty LP2 text segments** into one GP29 index stream, including transitions across segment boundaries. We used those same bytes and source alphabet. The new control matches stream length, alphabet size, and total adjacent-repeat count. It does **not** match each page, unigram frequency, word boundaries, or other structure. We designed it *after* seeing the source's first-order anomaly, so it is a diagnostic of that anomaly, not a new discovery test. The suggested larger filtered-control and held-out PPM campaigns remain open.

## Reproduce

The [source replay plan](experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/source-plan-as-frozen.json) and [diagnostic plan](experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/diagnostic-plan.json) pin their separate scopes. With a checkout of the [pinned revision](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1), run from the Liberpedia repository root:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/run.py --source-root SOURCE
python experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/diagnostic.py --source-root SOURCE --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/check.py --source-root SOURCE
python experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/plot.py --check
```

The [source result](experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/source-mdl_result.json), [fresh replay](experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/replayed-mdl_result.json), and [1,000 diagnostic rows](experiments/records/dukotah-mdl-order-profile/diagnostic-results.json) are retained. The independent checker recalculates every reported entropy from raw rune transitions.

records.title: Two language-scoring controls missed their frozen rules
records.question: Did two archived language-scoring searches satisfy their own frozen positive-control rules?
records.summary: Both sources report 20,480 manuscript decodes, but neither saved control meets its preregistered advantage-over-English test. Each program used a different comparison to proceed.

record_type.label: Source or input audit
record_type.description: Checks image provenance, extraction or input coverage against a declared reference; it does not establish a decryption.

scope.representation: Two pinned Dukotah source-control audits: R24-C1-ext four language-specific models and R24-C1 matched-runic orthography-adjusted English scorer. Each has a frozen plan, decision code and saved 24-plant control summaries. No manuscript grid was locally rerun.
scope.procedure: Verify source file hashes; recompute each frozen own-null power decision and the different executed decision from all eligible saved control summaries; distinguish the two scoring models and compare their source verdicts.
scope.parameters: R24-C1-ext: Latin, Greek, Old English and Enochian, 24 plants and 60 wrong-key controls each. R24-C1 matched: Latin, Greek and vowel-dropped English at L=120, 24 plants each. Each source reports a separate 20,480-case LP2 grid; neither grid was locally rerun.
scope.exclusions: No conclusion about actual plaintext language, the entire key family, numeric manuscript scores, other source registers, or changed control designs. The orthography-matched English scorer is not a language-specific model.

records.finding: Four language-specific models all tied English at 24/24 plants under the frozen own-null detection-rate rule; the program instead passed them by d-prime. A separate orthography-matched English scorer also tied ordinary English under its frozen rule on Latin, Greek and vowel-dropped English; its program passed Latin via an OR with a fixed-score-bar comparison. Neither reported zero-survivor manuscript grid is control-validated under its original rule.
records.limitations: This independently checks pinned plans, decision code and saved control summaries from two source lanes. Neither planted simulation nor either reported 20,480-case manuscript grid was locally rerun. An orthography-matched English scorer is not a Latin or Greek language model; no actual plaintext language is established.
records.article:
Two archived searches each report 20,480 Liber Primus decodes and no surviving candidate. Each set a positive-control rule before searching: its proposed scorer had to detect planted text **more often than the English scorer** when each was compared with its own wrong-key controls. Neither saved control meets that rule. Both programs used a different comparison to continue.

**Four language models.** The [frozen plan](experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/source-PREREG.md) tests Latin, Greek, Old English and Enochian models. **Zero of four** beat English on detection rate: both scorers find all 24 plants in every language. The program instead uses a standardized-score difference (*d-prime*) and passes all four.

**Matched rune spelling.** A [separate plan](experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/sibling-matched/source-PREREG.md) tests an **English** quadgram scorer adjusted for rune spelling. **Zero of three** eligible controls beat ordinary English against each scorer’s own wrong-key maximum. Latin and Greek are 24/24 under both; vowel-dropped English is 0/24 under both. The program also checks a fixed −5.5 score bar. At that bar, Latin rises from 12/24 to 19/24, so the program passes it through an OR condition.

![The four language-model controls tie English on every planted passage.](experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/control-gate.svg)

The two tests answer different questions. The first uses models trained for other languages. The second changes how an English model handles rune spelling; its improvement at a fixed bar does **not** turn it into a Latin or Greek language model. The saved rates show no advantage under either test’s frozen *own-null detection-rate* rule. The changed comparisons may be useful diagnostics, but they were not the declared pass criteria.

The original [language-model program](experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/source-control.py) uses d-prime to mark four registers validated. The separate [matched-runic program](experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/sibling-matched/source-control.py) uses the own-null result **or** a fixed-bar result, marking Latin validated. These are checks of the pinned plans, source decisions and saved control rows. **We did not rerun either planted simulation or either 20,480-case manuscript search.** Their reported zero survivors therefore cannot be presented as exclusions validated under their original control rules. The audits do not establish what language, if any, the unsolved pages contain.

## Check the controls

From the repository root, run:

```bash
python experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-nonenglish-control-gate/sibling-matched/check.py --check
```

The first checker compares all four saved language-model rows with both decision rules. The second verifies the pinned sibling source bytes and recomputes the frozen and executed decisions for Latin, Greek and vowel-dropped English. Source plans, code and saved receipts are bundled under the source repository’s MIT license. A new search would need a predeclared control that can reveal a detection-rate advantage, followed by one unchanged decision rule and a matched null for the full search.

records.title: The offset screen changes when training books are missing
records.question: Do matching planted-control totals mean a fallback prefilter selects the same key offsets as the pinned four-book source model?
records.summary: Yes. Both kept 26 of 40 planted true offsets, but five individual trial rankings changed; the first-ranked count was 21 versus 22, and one full million-offset target unit chose a different best position.

record_type.label: Control
record_type.description: Checks a search, decoder or scorer using synthetic inputs or reference text; it does not identify the cipher of an unsolved page.

scope.representation: The source 12,956-rune unsolved stream supplies the first 24-rune screening window and 400-rune beam head in one A1 unit; forty source-planted 372-rune English messages test offset recovery. This record makes no page-wide solving claim.
scope.procedure: Rebuild the fallback 29^3 trigram table independently from pinned KJV; verify four book hash gates; recount paired source/fallback control rows; compare one complete 2^20-offset A1 source checkpoint with a changed-model pilot.
scope.parameters: 40 paired source/fallback planted controls; 1,048,576 offsets in A1 unit 0; GP29, 24-rune screen, 400-rune head, max_skip 8. Archived C2 300-row summaries and offset totals are supporting saved-output arithmetic only.
scope.exclusions: No exact four-book model reconstruction, no fresh full A1/A2 or Marsaglia sweep, no new negative LP2 key verdict, no general statement that all scorer variants disagree.

records.finding: The exact source builder/sharding audit passed on locally available inputs. A KJV-only retraining independently rebuilds the fallback trigram cache. Both source and fallback controls recovered 40/40 planted messages and retained 26/40 true offsets; only 35/40 complete trial rows matched. Source ranked the true offset first 21/40 times, fallback 22/40. A1 unit 0 chose offset 400,310 in the archived four-book source checkpoint and 673,662 with the fallback model.
records.limitations: This is a retrospective instrument/input control, not an LP2 decryption or a source-exact replay of the full L6 sweep. The pinned Moby-Dick and Pride and Prejudice bytes are absent; their current official downloads fail the capsule hashes, and the 1.2 GB Marsaglia files are absent. The single changed A1 unit does not isolate model drift from every possible environment difference. Archived C2/offset arithmetic was recounted from saved output, not fresh pad scans.
records.article:
# Matching control totals can hide a different scorer

The public offset search screens millions of possible key positions before trying its decoder. That screen learns rune patterns from four books. In the available checkout, three training books were missing, so the source code quietly built a different screen from the KJV alone.

The source and fallback both recovered the known message in **40/40** planted trials and both kept its true offset in **26/40**. Those totals look reassuring. The individual rankings changed in **5 of 40** trials; the true offset ranked first in **21** source trials and **22** fallback trials. When we reran one of the source's million-offset target units, its best offset changed from **400,310** to **673,662**. The scores changed too. Matching control totals therefore do not establish that the same candidates reached the decoder.

![Source and KJV-only controls kept the same number of true offsets, but ranked different ones first.](experiments/records/dukotah-offset-model-integrity/comparison.svg)

This is an input and instrument check, **not a result about an LP2 key**. The original converter, sharding, and planted beam checks passed on the available inputs. An independent reconstruction matched the saved KJV-only trigram table exactly. The source's four-book model cannot be rebuilt from this checkout: the pinned hashes match KJV and *War and Peace*, while current official *Moby-Dick* and *Pride and Prejudice* downloads differ. Newline and BOM variants, plus an existing cached *Pride and Prejudice* file, did not restore the pinned bytes.

The separately archived C2 trial counts, offset-coverage fractions, and Marsaglia case-space arithmetic also recount correctly from their saved rows. That is an **arithmetic check of saved output**. The 1.2 GB of source Marsaglia pad data are gitignored and absent here, so their hashes and pad scans were not replayed. We cannot present the source's large negative sweep totals as independently reproduced under the exact screening model.

Run `python -X utf8 experiments/records/dukotah-offset-model-integrity/check.py` to verify the bundled input hashes, independently rebuild the fallback model from KJV, recount all 40 trial rows, and compare the pinned A1 checkpoint. NumPy is required. Run `python -X utf8 experiments/records/dukotah-offset-model-integrity/plot.py --check` to verify the figure. The retrospective [plan](experiments/records/dukotah-offset-model-integrity/plan.json) lists every exact input and explicitly does not claim advance registration.

To rerun the source code offline, use `python -X utf8 experiments/records/dukotah-offset-model-integrity/replay.py --controls-only` for all 40 planted trials. Omit `--controls-only` to also run the preselected million-offset A1 unit. The harness reconstructs the source tree in a temporary folder from bundled, hash-checked files, supplies the exact source ciphertext bytes, and compares fresh output with the saved KJV-only receipts; it never changes the pinned source or fetches another book.

The source rules and archived results are pinned to [Dukotah/cicada3301 at f08b20b](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round18/L6-offset-marsaglia). To replay the original full offset or Marsaglia searches, first restore the exact four scorer books and pad bytes, verify their hashes, then run the source controls and target grids unchanged.
records.reader_finding: The one-book screen passed the same headline controls as the original, but ranked five of the 40 trials differently. It also selected a different best key position in one search unit.
records.reader_limit: This does not reproduce the original four-book search or identify an LP2 key. Two exact training books and the separate random-pad archive remain unavailable.

records.title: What does the low-n ornament filter count?
records.question: Do fresh image component counts reproduce the stored counts in the 30 ornament boxes selected by n <= 16?
records.summary: Exact-image recount reproduces all 30 stored component counts. The old n <= 16 selection does not mean at most sixteen glyphs.

record_type.label: Manuscript measurement
record_type.description: Measures a stated feature or statistical comparison; it does not test a complete decoding rule.

family.title: Ornament component counts
family.question: What do the catalogue counts measure in the source image boxes?

variant.label: Pinned source scope and controls

scope.representation: 19 exact JPEGs and all 30 low-n source inventory boxes; pinned source counts and component geometry functions.
scope.procedure: Whole-page Pillow L conversion, ink <128; 4-connected components; area >=6 pixels; select component bounding boxes with positive x/y overlap and overlap rectangle area >= half component bounding rectangle area. End coordinates exclusive as scipy find_objects.
scope.parameters: Threshold <128; 4-connectivity; area >=6; overlap bounding rectangle >=50%; original coordinates frozen before measurement.
scope.exclusions: Glyph naming, template matching, reading or decoding ornament bands, hidden-content exclusion, and the other 79 source boxes.

records.finding: All 30 fresh component counts match stored n_components. Nine match n_reported, thirteen exceed 16, and the fresh range is 0–341 across 19 byte-verified JPEGs.
records.limitations: Component topology is not glyph segmentation. Only the frozen 30 boxes were measured. No templates or band reading were used; the separate 83.4% fresh-reader gate remains failed. This does not assess hidden content.
records.article:
The frozen P-9 selection contains all 30 inventory boxes whose original n field is at most 16. A fresh count from 19 JPEGs matches the source's stored n_components in every box. Only 9 boxes match the old n field; 13 have more than 16 connected components. The fresh range is 0 to 341.

This measures a field-definition mismatch. The inventory's old n is an upstream catalogue field, not a validated glyph count. Connected components are also not glyph counts: touching strokes can merge, detached parts can split, and edge selection can omit ink. The measurement does not establish how many runes any box contains.

Before segmentation, plan.json froze all selected IDs, coordinates, expected JPEG hashes, parameters and stop rules. All 19 local images matched the pinned source target_renders SHA-256 values. run.py independently implements whole-page grayscale thresholding below 128, four-connected segmentation, minimum ink area six pixels, and the source's bounding-box overlap selection of at least half the component bounding rectangle area. Coordinates use exclusive component stops exactly as scipy.find_objects does.

check.py uses Python AST selection to execute only page_ink, labelled and comp_table from the bundled hash-verified reader source. It compares every selected component rectangle and pixel area with the independent run, then checks the stored counts. It does not import the full reader, load its missing templates, or run its glyph decoder. A small synthetic topology/minimum-area control is also checked. The source snapshot is pinned to f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1.

These exact image measurements support the saved component counts and reject treating the old low-n filter as a count of at most sixteen glyphs. They do not support the stronger source verdict that a hidden artwork channel is absent. The separate fresh ornament reader gate reached 83.4%, below its 90% threshold, so no band text reading or decoding is attempted here. A new validated reader and appropriate controls would be needed for a content test.

Reproduce offline from the repository root after supplying the declared original image bundle:

    python experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-component-recount/run.py --check
    python experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-component-recount/check.py
    python experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-component-recount/plot.py --check
records.reader_finding: The low-n field is not a glyph count. Fresh image counts match all 30 stored component counts, but only 9 match the old n field; 13 boxes exceed 16 components.
records.reader_limit: Connected ink components do not identify glyphs or rule out hidden content. No band decoding was run.

records.title: Can the rebuilt reader inspect ornament bands?
records.question: Does the fresh 229-class image reader pass the source's direct solved-page control before it is used on artwork-adjacent bands?
records.summary: The fresh image reader reaches 83.4% agreement on two held-out solved LP2 pages, below the source's 90% calibration gate. Ornament content was not evaluated with it.

record_type.label: Source or input audit
record_type.description: Checks image provenance, extraction or input coverage against a declared reference; it does not establish a decryption.

records.article:
# Can the rebuilt reader inspect the ornament bands?

The [A-06 source method](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round18/L3-ornaments) proposes reading artwork-adjacent bands with an image-to-rune reader. Its historical **226-class** template file is unavailable. We instead tried the same raw reader with a [freshly rebuilt 229-class bank](experiments/records/dukotah-image-template-rebuild/article.md), clearly as a **new variant**.

## First, can it read known text?

![The fresh raw reader matches 85.4% on LP2-56 and 81.7% on LP2-57; both miss the source's 90% gate.](experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/solved-reader-gate.svg)

We applied the source's page-reading code directly to the two solved LP2 images, with no supplied rune positions or line lengths. The fresh class-to-rune mapping was fitted on LP2-00–55; **neither solved page was in that fit**. The reader matched **82 of 96** compared positions on LP2-56 and **89 of 109** on LP2-57: **171 of 205, or 83.4% combined**. The source's required calibration is **90%**. It also emitted more runes than the visible text on both pages (96 versus 85; 109 versus 95).

This differs from the [T2 substitution probe](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/article.md), which scored 178 of 178 solved-page rune choices **with the surrounding reference text and positions supplied**. That useful control does not show that the reader can independently extract a line of runes from pixels. The raw-reader result here tests that harder prerequisite.

Because the control failed, **we did not read the ornament bands or score the source's hidden-message hypotheses** with this fresh bank. The archived source inventory still gives coordinates for **109 candidate bands on 39 pages**; that is a list of image regions, not 109 decoded strings. The result says the current fresh reader is not calibrated for a negative finding about those bands. It says nothing about whether artwork contains a message.

## One transcription difference

At rune 80 (zero-based) on LP2-57, the pinned source markdown has `E` in `...DIUINITE...`; Liberpedia's page text has `Y` in `...DIUINITY...`. The rune is on the fifth runic row near image coordinate **(932, 1725)**. The [original page image](images/lp2-57.jpg) and our [row crop](experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/lp2-57-line5-crop.png) show the **Y-shaped rune**; the raw reader also outputs `Y` there. The primary score above uses the source's own text. Using Liberpedia's reading changes only this comparison, to **172 of 205 (83.9%)**—still below the gate. Neither transcription was silently changed.

## Reproduce

The [frozen variant plan](experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/variant-plan.json) pins the source revision, fresh bank, both canonical inputs, images and gate before any band-content reading. From the Liberpedia root, with Python, NumPy, SciPy and Pillow, plus the [original images](downloads/original-images.zip) extracted into `images/`:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/run_gate.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/plot.py --check
```

The [full predicted and reference rune arrays](experiments/records/dukotah-ornament-fresh-reader-gate/gate-results.json) support an independent recount. This fresh-bank test cannot reproduce the source's missing historical template file or its archived ornament verdict.

records.article:
# Can the number-grid bytes act as a key when key positions are skipped?

**Finding.** We reran a published decoder that treats the 256 bytes derived from the LP2-49–51 number grid as a repeating key. It permits a key position to be skipped when that position would have repeated the previous ciphertext rune. Across **880 fixed page and key settings**, no output reached the program’s English-score bar. The best score was **−6.756 on LP2-15**, below its **−5.5** bar. A separate implementation reproduced every decoded path and score.

The decoder can recover a known message under these rules: when we encrypted the complete **85-rune LP2-56 reading** with each payload, sign and Atbash setting, it returned the exact reading in **16 of 16** planted cases. That makes the no-hit result informative for this fixed search, while leaving other key construction rules open.

![The sixteen planted known readings clear the source's English-score bar and recover exactly. The highest-scoring manuscript setting remains below the bar.](experiments/records/dukotah-payload-key-skip/comparison.svg)

| What entered the decoder | Complete known text recovered | Above the source score bar |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Planted 85-rune reading | **16/16** | **16/16** |
| Unsolved manuscript pages | Unknown | **0/880** |

The score rates how closely the continuous rune transliteration resembles English four-letter patterns. Passing it is a search screen, not proof of a correct reading. In the planted cases we also compared **every rune** with the known text. The best manuscript case starts `EAEASYDANGYEALT…`; isolated letter-like fragments are not a decoded passage.

## What was tried

The source provides **two distinct 256-byte readings** of the LP2-49–51 grid. Each was tested forward and backward. Every byte becomes its remainder modulo 29, producing four candidate key streams. For each stream, the program tried both addition directions, with and without Atbash, at key offset zero on each of the **55 rune-bearing pages LP2-00–55**. LP2-50 has no transcribed alphabet runes and is skipped. The grid is therefore **4 streams × 2 signs × 2 Atbash choices × 55 pages = 880 settings**.

At each rune the beam considers the next key value or as many as three extra advances. An advance is allowed only if each bypassed value would have made the preceding ciphertext rune repeat. It keeps the 320 highest-scoring paths and chooses a complete page output. The exact source script does **not** run the whole-book branch described in its introductory comment; this replay covers its executable page loop only.

The 55 source rune arrays match the corresponding Liberpedia page records exactly, including the page-number shift after rune-free LP2-50. The original program reproduces its preserved output: the winning setting is the first byte reading, subtraction, Atbash, LP2-15. Our separate scalar decoder agrees on **all 880 full-length paths**, not only that winner.

There is an important boundary on the key model. For pages longer than 256 runes, the source repeats the payload enough to cover the page’s initial length. Its beam then pads with **zero key values** if a hypothetical skip path runs beyond the allocated key array. We preserved that executable behavior. This result does not test an indefinitely repeating 256-byte stream for every possible skip path.

The source’s broader generic validation script also calls for an unrelated `mabinogion.txt` as a wrong-key check. That file is absent from the pinned repository, so the generic gate stops before its wrong-key condition. Its correct-key part recovers **212/212** planted runes; the **payload-specific** full-reading controls above pass independently. We do not report the incomplete generic gate as passed.

## Reproduce

The [plan frozen before the manuscript rerun](experiments/records/dukotah-payload-key-skip/plan-frozen.json) fixes the source revision, grid, bar and controls. The [per-setting results](experiments/records/dukotah-payload-key-skip/results.json) include page labels, scores and hashes of every complete decoded path. Run these from a Liberpedia checkout:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-payload-key-skip/run.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-payload-key-skip/check.py
```

The first command runs the [pinned Campaign XVIII source](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/corpus/H-branch-recovery/recovered/claude_master-roadmap-libra-qk527u/liber-primus/analysis/campaign18_skip/payload_skip.py) in a temporary directory and compares its report with the preserved log. The second independently reconstructs all page arrays, scoring, 880 beam outputs and 16 complete-message controls. Exact source code and inputs are bundled under the source project’s MIT license. The result concerns **this payload-as-key rule**; it does not evaluate every key one could derive from the number grid or the other Campaign XVIII branches.

records.article:
# Can the LP2 grid bytes describe doublet gaps?

The [source's E‑02v test](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round28/L5/PREREG.md) treats the 256-byte LP2-49–51 grid payload as a sequence of base-128 integers. It asks whether those integers rise and fall with the distances between adjacent repeated runes elsewhere in LP2. This extends our [earlier seven-reading check](#/experiments/payload-doublet-gaps) to the source's **three byte versions and all 24 stated comparisons**.

![Across three pinned byte versions, the strongest rank correlations are 0.119, 0.119 and 0.117, far below the source's 0.5 gate.](experiments/records/dukotah-payload-varint-matrix/varint-gap-matrix.svg)

**All 24 rows reproduce the source's saved result; none reaches its stated effect-size gate.** Each byte version was decoded as both LEB128 and MSB-first base 128, reading bytes forward or backward. Each of those four streams was compared with 85 distances between repeated-rune events and with a related 86-value sequence that starts at the first event's position. The strongest absolute Spearman rank correlation is **0.1187**, against a required **greater than 0.5**. Because no row crosses that first gate, the source's 100,000-permutation second stage is not invoked.

This tests a specific *numeric reading* of the grid, not whether repeated runes matter or whether the payload encodes something else. The three byte versions differ, but their best correlations are nearly identical. The [complete row table](experiments/records/dukotah-payload-varint-matrix/results.json) preserves decoded lengths, compared lengths and signed correlations, so the small differences are inspectable.

## How it was checked

The four pinned inputs are exact source bytes: three 256-byte payload versions and its 12,956-byte LP2 rune stream. That stream has 86 adjacent repeat events; their 85 distances start **85, 249, 197, 129, 127**. We independently decoded and ranked each of the 24 cases, then compared each rounded row with the source's archived output. The original source reports **10/10** planted gap-sequence recoveries and **0/50** random-payload hits. Our separate positive check re-encodes all 85 real gaps in both base-128 orders, recovers them exactly and obtains correlation 1.

The [local plan](experiments/records/dukotah-payload-varint-matrix/plan.json) fixes inputs and rules for this replay, but it follows an already published source result; it is **not an independent preregistration**. The source's controls are archived receipts, whereas our positive check and independent 24-row recount were run here. Arbitrary byte transformations, start offsets, gap definitions and cipher mechanisms remain outside the test.

Run from the repository root with Python 3:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-payload-varint-matrix/run.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-payload-varint-matrix/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-payload-varint-matrix/plot.py
```

records.article:
# Reading directions with simple ciphers

Could changing the order of a page's lines and then applying a familiar cipher reveal a complete passage? A pinned Campaign VII program tried five reading orders with 37 fixed cipher settings. We replayed all **10,175 complete outputs** on its 55 unsolved rune-bearing pages. **No output reached the source's fixed −5 quadgram-score threshold.** Its best page scored **−6.717**; the known *Parable* reading scored **−4.421** on the same scale. In 49 complete shuffled searches, **40** found a best score at least as high as the manuscript's. Higher scores are more English-like under this particular model; the threshold does not by itself certify a readable passage.

![The best manuscript output sits among complete shuffled-search results, while the known reading is far higher.](experiments/records/dukotah-reading-direction-cipher-grid/comparison.svg)

| Reading order | What happens to a page |
| --- | --- |
| Rows | Read lines in their archived order. |
| Reverse | Reverse the complete rune sequence. |
| Alternating rows | Reverse every other line. |
| Columns | Read down ordinal rune positions; skip missing positions in short lines. |
| Reverse columns | Reverse that column output. |

Each route is followed by direct reading, Atbash, 28 nonzero shifts, both arithmetic signs for three prime-related streams, and subtraction of a repeating `DIVINITY` key. This is **one grouped search of fixed settings**, not thousands of different ideas. The [source program](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/corpus/H-branch-recovery/recovered/claude_master-roadmap-libra-qk527u/liber-primus/analysis/campaign7/reading_direction.py) and its [archived result](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/corpus/H-branch-recovery/recovered/claude_master-roadmap-libra-qk527u/liber-primus/analysis/campaign7/reading_direction_results.json) fix the methods and model. The original program did **not** run our 49 shuffle comparisons; those are an added whole-search control.

The best unsolved output came from [LP2-49](#/reader/lp2-49): reverse its ordinal-column reading, then subtract seven from every rune index. Its opening is `NJLTDIGNORWEOFTNGCOBSEOE...`, not a coherent passage. This is the exact program winner, not a visually selected fragment. The archived source's winner and the best score for every route match our replay after its three-decimal rounding.

The program's source text has 55 nonempty unsolved segments; LP2-50 has an alphanumeric grid but no transcribed runes, so the source skips that segment and source segment 50 corresponds to LP2-51. All 57 source segments, including LP2-56 and LP2-57, match the site's archived rune sequences exactly under that mapping. The source's straight-through LP2-57 *Parable* passes its −5 threshold. LP2-56 is a known **enciphered** page and does not pass by direct reading, so it is not treated as a direct-English positive. We additionally encrypted the *Parable* page with shift seven and rearranged it into both alternating-row and ordinal-column layouts. The declared routes recovered every rune and crossed the threshold. These plants check the machinery on a readable text, not its power for every conceivable manuscript reading.

The shuffle control preserves each page's rune counts and line lengths, then repeats the **entire 10,175-setting search** before taking one best score. Its median maximum was **−6.625**. The manuscript's −6.717 is lower than 40 of the 49 control maxima; the one-sided empirical estimate with a +1 correction is **41/50 = 0.82**. This does not establish a cipher model or a universal probability of a reading. It shows that the source's best score is not unusual for this specified search and simple null.

This result is limited to these five layout conventions, these 37 cipher settings, the complete source pages, and one English quadgram scorer. It does not close physical image-coordinate routes, a rule for selecting only some runes, other keys, resets, or non-English passages. The earlier [pure row/column route test](#/experiments/lp2-row-column-routes) tested opening matches without a cipher; this record adds the exact archived route-plus-cipher grid.

The [plan](experiments/records/dukotah-reading-direction-cipher-grid/plan.json) freezes the source bytes and added controls. The [results](experiments/records/dukotah-reading-direction-cipher-grid/results.json) include each page's winning setting and all 49 complete-search controls. From a checkout or extracted bundle, run:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-reading-direction-cipher-grid/run.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-reading-direction-cipher-grid/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-reading-direction-cipher-grid/plot.py --check
```

The checker separately parses the source text, reconstructs the five traversals and 37 transformations, and recomputes every grid maximum. Its floating-point score comparisons use a tight tolerance because its summation path differs from the source's.

records.article:
## Finding

**The original T2 control programs run on the newly pinned image templates, and their planted changes are usually found.** All **545 valid physical rune splices** were detected and read correctly. Of 604 planted missing runes, **598** were localized; of 604 planted extra runes, **588** were localized. These are strong results for these specific one-change plants. They do not establish that the manuscript has at most one transcription error.

![The physical splice and planted length-error controls recover most synthetic changes, while 26 unplanted lines remain flagged and a separator plant control is missing.](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/figure.svg)

This follow-up uses the [fresh 229-class image bank](#/experiments/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo) and the [pinned source T2 programs](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round19/T2). The original archived bank reported 226 classes; its arrays are unavailable. The source's shorthand “segments 45–54” means manuscript pages **LP2-45–49 and LP2-51–55** here, since LP2-50 has no rune lines.

| Source control | What happened | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1, solved pages | 178/178 local rune choices agree | The substitution probe passes its 90% entry gate. |
| C2′, physical splice | 545/545 valid planted runes recovered; 189/189 in source segments 45–54 | Its dense-segment recovery exceeds the registered 50% gate. |
| C5, planted missing rune | 598/604 localized | The length probe often recovers a single missing-rune plant. |
| C5, planted extra rune | 588/604 localized | The length probe often finds a single extra-rune plant. |

The splice code requests 200 placements in each of three groups. Some replacement runes do not fit the erased glyph span: **4,774 of 16,184** proposed slot–rune pairs were excluded, leaving 168 solved-page, 189 dense-segment and 188 other valid splices. The high recovery applies to this width-filtered sample.

## What the manuscript measurements say

Using thresholds set from the solved pages, the indel program flags **26 unplanted lines**: 24 on LP2-00–44 and two on LP2-53. It flags none on the solved pages. The source then labels every flag “segmentation” using the direction of a component-count mismatch or equality with the canonical rune count. The [individual flagged rows](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/out_indel_adj.json) remain available for inspection.

That classification is a **rule applied to image components**, not a ground-truth reading of every flagged rune. Equal component and reference counts cannot rule out a merged pair, a split stroke, or offsetting insertion and deletion. The source's stated 95% bound of at most one real insertion or deletion additionally assumes that synthetic single-error localization transfers to unknown real errors and that detections are independent. This replay verifies the program's plants and arithmetic, but not those assumptions. It therefore **does not certify the number of real transcription errors**.

The separator script reports exact *counts* on **582/604** lines and exact *positions* on **580/604**, including **10/10** solved lines. The **19 older disputed-count lines** now have matching counts under this newer mark classifier. Its `sep19.py` calls these “alignment” cases solely because the counts agree; that label is not an independent manual check of the pixels. The registered C4 control—delete one separator on ten solved lines and require 8/10 lower residuals—has no implementation in the pinned T2 scripts and **was not run**.

## Reproduce

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/plan.json) pins the source revision, image/instrument dependencies and control order. The [results](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/results.json) link every raw output hash. The independent receipt checker recounts the 545 splices, 1,208 indel plants, 26 flags and separator totals from the saved rows without calling the source's image code:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/check.py
```

For a full rerun, use Python with NumPy, SciPy and Pillow and the [pinned source revision](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round19/T2). The wrapper verifies source code, all 58 original JPEGs and the fresh instrument, then runs the original scripts in an isolated temporary tree. `--controls-only` uses the bundled, hash-pinned fresh line map and substitution probe; `--rebuild` recomputes those first. Both enforce the solved and dense splice gates before later controls:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/run.py --source-root PATH/TO/liber-primus --site-root . --controls-only --check
```

The original scripts' raw [splice](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/out_splice.json), [indel](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/out_indel.json) and [separator](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-controls/out_separators.json) results are preserved, including the flagged cases and every tested plant. The wrapper compares parsed JSON so platform newline differences do not change the scientific result.
When replaying the bundled Windows line map on a Unix host, the wrapper changes only its filesystem path separators in the temporary copy; line identities and measurements stay fixed.

## Finding

**A fresh image-template bank makes the same rune choices as the archived T2 probe on all 604 lines.** The two runs do not have identical measurements: their candidate costs differ on **329 lines**, and selected image positions differ on **262**. The ten solved LP2 lines pass the source's first control, with **178 of 178** tested positions agreeing with the documented reading.

![All 604 lines retain the same best rune sequence, while costs and measured positions change on many lines.](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/figure.svg)

This is a **fresh variant of the original substitution probe**, using the 229-class template bank rebuilt in [the image-pipeline audit](#/experiments/dukotah-image-template-rebuild). The archived T2 bank reported 226 classes, and its original arrays are unavailable. Identical rune choices do not mean that the historical image measurements were reproduced exactly.

## What was tested

The [pinned T2 program](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus/analysis/round19/T2) aligns each manuscript line against a reference rune sequence. It then temporarily opens one position, compares the 29 possible rune labels at that position, and restores the reference labels around it. We ran its original line mapper and substitution probe on **58 byte-matched JPEGs**: LP2-00–55 and the two solved pages LP2-56–57. No thresholds or source algorithms were changed.

The solved-page control was run **before** the full probe. Those ten lines were absent from the fresh class-to-rune label fit, so this control is held out from that fit. The probe still uses each line's reference length and neighboring rune labels. Agreement on the unsolved pages therefore tests local consistency with the supplied transcription; it is **not an independent reading of those pages from pixels**.

| Page group | Tested positions | Same as reference | Different choices |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| LP2-00–44 | 10,951 | 10,916 | 35 |
| LP2-45–49 and LP2-51–55 | 1,992 | 1,992 | 0 |
| Solved LP2-56–57 | 178 | 178 | 0 |

The archived and fresh probes also agree on the *best rune sequence* for every one of the 604 lines, including the 35 positions where that sequence differs from the reference. That stability is useful evidence about this particular local substitution test. It does not settle disputed word breaks, insertions, deletions, or manuscript transcription as a whole. The source's separate physical-splice, indel and separator controls were not rerun here.

The source calls the 91-line group “segments 45–54.” Its page mapping skips runeless LP2-50: these segments correspond to manuscript pages **45–49 and 51–55**. The checker asserts that mapping for every compact row.

## Reproduce

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/plan.json) lists the 58 image hashes, source revision, source program hashes and the fresh instrument hashes. The [compact line receipt](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/line-results.json) preserves each line's reference and best rune indices, candidate costs and positions for both runs. The independent checker recounts all 13,121 comparisons and the source-versus-fresh differences without calling T2's scoring code:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/check.py
```

To rerun the original source programs, obtain the [pinned source revision](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/liber-primus), then use Python with NumPy, SciPy and Pillow. The wrapper checks all image, source and instrument hashes, creates an isolated temporary tree, runs the solved-page gate first and only then runs all pages. It does not alter the source checkout or saved receipts:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/run.py --source-root PATH/TO/liber-primus --site-root . --rebuild --check
```

The same wrapper can compare an already generated isolated source tree with the saved receipt using `--artifact-root PATH/TO/isolated/liber-primus --check`. The bundled [template bank](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/templates.npz) and [class mapping](experiments/records/dukotah-t2-fresh-template-loo/diff_report.json) fix the *fresh* instrument exactly; they do not substitute for the missing historical NPZ.

records.article:
# Word boundaries as key clocks

These three archived search branches ask whether the visible separators and words control a shifting key. We replayed the exact source rules on all 55 rune-bearing unsolved LP2 pages, then compared each branch's best score with **49 shuffled searches that repeated the entire branch**. None of the manuscript bests crossed the source's fixed −5 English quadgram threshold. The highest score from any branch, −6.897, was matched or exceeded by 44 of the 49 shuffled *combined* searches.

![Three short bars show the number of shuffled searches that reached or exceeded each manuscript score. A note shows that the archived known-page candidate matches 56 of 85 runes, then diverges.](experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/comparison.svg)

| Source branch | What moves the key | Best unsolved score | Shuffled searches at least as high |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| FH1 · separator clock | A chosen `-`, `.`, or `/` advances the stream without printing a rune | −6.904, LP2-14 | 23/49 |
| FH3 · punctuation reset | A selected word, clause, line, or segment mark restarts the stream | −7.008, LP2-51 | 43/49 |
| W1–W5 · word sums | GP-prime values of the previous word, or the previous rune, supply the next key value | −6.897, LP2-49 | 37/49 |

**The known-reading check changes how to read this result.** The archived FH3 report highlights an `AN END WITHIN THE DEEP WEB...` opening on source page 55 (LP2-56). We compared its *entire* 85-rune output with the documented reading. The first 56 positions match; rune 57 differs, and the full text is **not** recovered. That candidate scores −5.282, below the source's own −5 threshold. A plausible opening is therefore not a passed known-page control. Seven synthetic examples did recover the complete known Parable reading when encrypted with these exact rules; they check the implementation, but they cannot show that the original ciphertext uses any of them.

## What was searched

FH1 used the source's three separator sets and four subtractive streams: primes, primes minus one, totients, and the repeating `DIVINITY` key. FH3 used four reset marks and three streams. The five word-sum variants used the 29-value Gematria Primus prime map. W1 uses the previous *ciphertext* word's prime sum, W2 the previous *decoded* word's sum, W3 the cumulative ciphertext-word sums, W4 the totient of the previous ciphertext-word sum, and W5 the previous ciphertext rune's prime value. Every W variant included both signs and both Atbash states, with a zero initial key. In the source parser, **any non-rune ends a word**.

That is 660 FH1 outputs, 660 FH3 outputs, and 1,100 word-sum outputs across the 55 unsolved source segments. The source omits the rune-free LP2-50 transcription segment. We checked the rune sequence of every other source segment against its site page. Source FH2 is a first-rune shift subset of the separately tested [whole-page affine family](#/experiments/wholepage-affine-gp29), so its archived winner is checked for source parity but not counted again here. FH4's proposed file relocation was not an executed cipher search.

The score is the archived mean English quadgram log score on the GP transliteration; a higher number means more English-like **under that model**, not a readable solution. The shuffled comparison preserves each page's rune inventory and every punctuation position. It repeats the full choice of stream, separator or word rule, sign, Atbash setting, and page before retaining the maximum. It measures selection effects under that shuffle, not the probability of a cipher model.

## What remains open

These results do not exclude a different initial state, a key from earlier pages, other separator meanings, a different language model, or a model that predicts the original punctuation. A new proposal can improve on this replay by fixing its key-clock rule before looking at the target page and recovering a complete known passage plus an untouched LP2 passage. The original 56-rune prefix should not be treated as a complete positive control.

## Reproduce and inspect

The [experiment plan](experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/plan.json) fixes the source revision, grid, controls, and exclusions. [Results](experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/results.json) contain every shuffle maximum and the exact source winners. The [replay](experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/run.py) checks the pinned programs and saved results; the [independent checker](experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/check.py) reconstructs all manuscript settings and shuffle maxima without importing those programs. Run:

```text
python experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/run.py --check
python experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/check.py
python experiments/records/dukotah-word-boundary-key-clocks/plot.py --check
```

The source scripts and their archived outputs are preserved under `source/` at commit `f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1`. The 49 full-grid shuffle controls and the full-reading comparison are **our added tests**, not results claimed by the archive. See the pinned [false-holes source](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/corpus/H-branch-recovery/recovered/claude_master-roadmap-libra-qk527u/liber-primus/analysis/campaign7/false_holes.py) and [word-sum source](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/f08b20b632d91209ddbaa747e8e2f23df0c78ba1/corpus/H-branch-recovery/recovered/claude_master-roadmap-libra-qk527u/liber-primus/analysis/campaign7/wordsum_selfkey.py).
