records.article:
# Could a mathematical sequence be the LP2 key?

**The specified number streams did not produce a reading under the tested model.** We replayed two public experiments that turn mathematical sequences into GP29 key values: fixed constants and concatenated numbers in [Stage AG](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_ag.py), and arithmetic functions in [Stage AH](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_ah.py). **None of the 19,140 scored settings met the source's reading threshold.** All 594 adequately long stream/alignment/mode groups met its exclusion rule. The remaining 66 groups use only *nine runes* from section 10, so they cannot settle much.

![No tested setting reached the reading threshold; the only undecided groups use nine runes.](experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/comparison.svg)

## The tested keys

Stage AG uses base-29 digits of π, e, φ, √2, √3, ln 2 and √3301, plus concatenated primes, positive integers and prime totients. Stage AH uses φ(n), divisor sums, cumulative totients, prime gaps, φ(φ(n)) and nφ(n), each directly and as a running sum, reduced modulo 29. That gives **22 named streams, 21 distinct streams**: the running sum of φ(n) is the same sequence as the direct cumulative-totient stream.

The source reads each key from one of **1,000 possible starting positions**, allowing occasional stays and skips so a small alignment error need not destroy a genuine signal. It tests three arithmetic directions and all 29 shifts on sections 7–15 individually, then on their joined stream. Its score asks whether the resulting rune frequencies look more like the solved LP1 readings than a flat-rune reference. The [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/plan.json) gives the exact settings and input hashes.

The source set **+30** as its reading threshold. For groups long enough to judge, the best score was **−47.85**, on section 7 using the running sum of φ(φ(n)); a positive score this far away was never reached. The best score over *all* settings was only **+1.76**, on section 10's nine runes. The source's exclusion criterion requires **all 29 shifts in a group to score at most −10**, with its planted controls working. It holds for every group outside that short section: **270/300** Stage AG groups and **324/360** Stage AH groups. The groups are model settings, not separate proposed solutions.

## Why the check is credible—and limited

For each named stream, the pinned program planted a known-key encryption at both 729 and 3,316 runes, with two key-continuation rules. All **88 positive controls** exceeded +30; the corresponding wrong-key controls stayed below it. We ran the complete source programs and compared all four [candidate and control tables](experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/results.json) byte-for-byte with the published tables. An [independent check](experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/check.py) rebuilds the 12,956-rune manuscript stream from Liberpedia's page files, checks the full parameter grid and controls, and verifies small arithmetic prefixes and the duplicate sequence.

This result concerns these **particular base-29 streams and the source's drift-tolerant frequency model**. It does not reject other numerical keys, different ways to turn a constant into runes, different boundaries or a cipher with a different plaintext distribution. Nor does a failure to reach the reading threshold establish that the manuscript was not constructed with mathematics.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, run `python experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/run.py --check` and `python experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/check.py`. The full upstream rerun needs a separate checkout of [Wulfic's repository](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus) at commit `bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c`, with its Python dependencies installed; run `python experiments/records/wulfic-number-key-streams/replay_source.py --source-dir PATH_TO_CLONE`. That wrapper checks the pinned source files, runs both stages into a temporary folder and compares their complete output tables with this archive.

records.article:
# Keys made from the P08 hint grid

The source calls its hint page **P08**; this is today's [LP1-08](#/wiki/2014-stage05), not LP2-08. An earlier [OutGuess extraction](#/wiki/outguess) from the original LP1-08 JPEG saved a 140-byte message. All **28 two-character groups** in its two grid rows match the [archived Wulfic script](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/p08_grid_analysis.py) in order. We checked the stored extraction against its recorded image and output hashes; this verifies the grid's provenance without treating the subsequent key idea as established.

The script converts each row's characters to Gematria Primus values and treats their differences or raw values as repeating keys. For example, its first `TL` / `SL` pair contributes **28, 0** to one 28-value key. We tested the script's seven fixed keys and the five keys it rotates through every phase.

**The threshold hits do not establish a reading.** The source's full old P08–54 range includes nine solved LP1 pages. Of **103** rotated-key hits above its index-of-coincidence cutoff, **99** are on those solved pages. The remaining **four** are on LP2-00–37, all on LP2-32. Three share one frequency relation: `KEY_A` subtraction and `KEY_B` addition give the same text, while `KEY_A` Beaufort reflects its alphabet and therefore has the same frequency score. The fourth uses a different raw-row key.

![Of 103 source cutoff hits, 99 occur on solved LP1 pages and 4 on unsolved LP2 pages. The strongest LP2 frequency score is a retrospective diagnostic, not a reading.](experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/comparison.svg)

Index of coincidence measures how often two rune positions carry the same rune; here it is scaled by 29. A high score measures concentration, not whether the rune order forms a readable message.

The strongest LP2 case is **1.382** on LP2-32, a 121-rune page. Its first 30 decoded runes transliterate as `LTHIOWRDBEOBNGTHJLBDOEWONJEAMFLBSEBTHF`. The reflected variant begins `NIOTHOEAEGEOBEOHIOENEOGWOEYLEUIFNEOXJEOIOF`; the other key begins `DCCYJNGUXSBTHCDNGPNGDDLBTHHGEOMHCNGCO`. These are candidate outputs for inspection, not verified plaintext. The source's own word score operates mostly on letter bigrams after removing the manuscript's word boundaries; it supplies no independent whole-page reading or held-out prediction.

The source's cutoff can detect the kind of text it seeks: we encrypted **17 established LP1 readings** with each of the five rotated keys at two phases and three directions. All **510** controls decrypted exactly and passed the same IoC cutoff. That tests the cutoff on those known-reading lengths, not on every possible language or layered cipher.

After seeing that the solved pages dominated, we examined LP2 separately using the **same 199 page shuffles** specified for the full sweep. None of the 199 shuffled LP2 maxima reached 1.382; **7 of 199** had at least four cutoff hits. This is explicitly a **post-observation subset diagnostic**. The shuffles preserve each page's rune counts but destroy position order. They do not model the full historical search over clues, keys and scoring choices, and zero observed shuffle exceedances does not imply zero chance or identify an encryptor.

The original script's page loader resolves to `tools/pages`, which contains no page files at the pinned commit. We corrected only that path and loaded the **47 committed `pages/page_08`–`page_54` Git blobs**. Under the modern page names these are LP1-08–16 and LP2-00–37. The corrected-path run has **987 fixed-key cases** (20 cutoff hits, all on solved LP1) and **17,766 rotated-key cases**. Its raw-input snapshot, all candidate scores, controls and both null readouts are bundled; it is an adaptation of the source's fixed arithmetic, not a claim that the legacy command itself ran as written.

This test covers the specified 14/28-value keys, three GP29 directions, and all source key phases on those pages. It leaves aside the same script's separate bigram-substitution, Koan-key and free arithmetic ideas, later LP2 pages, other hint encodings and other reading criteria. See the [carrier comparison](experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/carrier-audit.json), [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/plan.json), [complete results](experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/results.json), and [LP2-only diagnostic plan](experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/diagnostic-plan.json).

To reproduce from the experiment ZIP or a full Liberpedia checkout with Python and NumPy:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/diagnostic.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/check.py
python experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/check_carrier.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-p08-hint-grid-keys/plot.py --check
```

The independent checker rebuilds every observed key from the source's paired rows, checks every source page array against its preserved raw bytes, and reevaluates all 18,753 observed cases and 510 planted controls. The seeded full-null replays are checked by the two complete run commands.

records.article:
# Do prime-position routes reveal a reading on LP2-03?

This [archived route program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/solve_p20.py) takes runes at **nonprime zero-based positions**, tries a Caesar shift, then reads that stream in 58 specified ways. The committed file called `page_20` is **LP2-03**, with **217 runes**, not the 646 stated in the program's opening comment. Its nonprime-position stream has 170 runes; the other 47 lie at prime positions.

## Result

The strongest route was an 11-column reading with **six hits** on the program's short list of English trigrams. When we shuffled the same 217 runes and repeated the *entire* split, shift and route search 199 times, **57 searches reached six or more**. This comparison gives no reason to single out the six-hit route as a reading. It is a descriptive control for this search and this spelling convention, not a model of every possible cipher.

![The best route has six trigram hits; 57 of 199 whole-search shuffles reached at least six.](experiments/records/wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes/comparison.svg)

The pinned program reports ten routes because nine are listed regardless of score and the 11-column route passes its `>5` gate. Its final ordering uses the *length of a formatted report string*, not a language score. The source also prints a distinct **prime rune-index-value split** (65/152); that is not the position split tested by these routes.

## Why the shift and routes need care

Every Caesar shift has the same index of coincidence: renaming the 29 symbols does not change their frequency counts. The program chooses shift zero on the first equal maximum; its displayed “best shift” is therefore not independent evidence for a key. Reversal and the complete column, diagonal, keyword and Deor sorts likewise preserve symbol frequencies. Prime-position sampling, fixed-step sampling, Fibonacci positions and padded spirals can change the stream or its length, so they are reported separately.

Before scoring the manuscript, a planted 170-rune message was recovered through the two-column route and passed the source's `>5` trigram gate. The unmodified staged source agreed with our route names and IoC values for every route it retained on that plant. Our independent checker later rebuilt **all 58** manuscript route sequences and digests, including routes below the source's reporting threshold. The predeclared goal of checking *every route against the unmodified source on synthetic inputs* was not fully met: the original program exposes only retained routes, so the source-parity control covered its retained synthetic rows; independent index-map reconstruction covered the rest. This distinction is in the saved receipts.

## Scope and reproduction

The runner uses the pinned Git bytes for `solve_p20.py`, `pages/page_20/runes.txt` and `data/corpora/deor_poem.txt`. It stages the source file unmodified in a temporary folder because its original Deor path differs from the committed path. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes/snapshot_inputs.py --source-root PATH --check`, then `gate.py --source-root PATH --check` and `run.py --source-root PATH --check`. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-p20-prime-position-routes/check.py` for the separate reconstruction.

The test covers those fixed routes on LP2-03 under the source's variable-length rune transliteration and trigram lists. It does not exclude other layouts, transcription choices, languages, or transposition rules. The related [Deor interlocking-stream test](#/experiments/wulfic-deor-interlocking-streams) splits on prime *rune-index values*, a different operation.

# Can selected F runes rescue these fixed keyword decodes?

The [archived second-layer program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/p21_30_second_layer.py) proposes one keyword and arithmetic direction for each of ten page files. For every ciphertext F rune, it tries two possibilities: decrypt it normally, or output a literal F and **pause key advancement**. The committed files `page_21`–`page_30` match current **LP2-04–13** rune for rune.

## Result

Across the ten pages, the program's bounds allow **27,402 F masks**. **None** makes every one-rune word an I or A under the program's own separator rule. The unmodified source consequently takes its fallback branch and chooses a mask by index of coincidence (IoC) on every page. That fallback is a frequency ranking, not a successful one-rune-word check.

![The best-IoC F mask raises concentration on some pages, while zero of 27,402 masks passes the required word gate.](experiments/records/wulfic-p21-literal-f-masks/comparison.svg)

The source's next stage tries **45 fixed rune routes per page** on the *ordinary no-mask* decode. None crosses its printing gates. It also prints prime-word, reversed-word and first-25-word magic-square views, but does not score those word orders. Reordering whole words cannot change how many individual words match a dictionary.

We repeated the full mask selection on 19 seeded rune-order shuffles of all ten pages, keeping each page's rune inventory and visible word slots. **All 19 also produced zero pages with an all-singleton-valid mask.** That comparison shows this strict gate has little ability to distinguish the actual pages under this control; it does not provide evidence for or against other F-skip rules.

## What was checked

Before using the manuscript, a planted 20-rune message with **two literal-F pauses** was recovered exactly and passed both one-rune-word checks. The source functions and a separate scalar recurrence agreed on 48 small mask/mode cases, and the compiled all-mask selector agreed on the plant. We then ran the unmodified source script against the exact committed page bytes. Its ten fallback choices match the saved scan. An independent scalar checker enumerates every manuscript mask again and reconstructs the first complete shuffled search.

The source's keyword parser is part of this result. It turns `DEOR` into three GP runes because `EO` is a digraph; it silently drops the `V` in `DIVINITY`, despite a comment that suggests `V` should map to `U`. We preserved that actual behavior. A corrected parser or a different keyword would be a new test. The source only treats period, hyphen, bullet, space and newline as word separators, so its singleton positions can differ from other transcriptions.

## Reproduce and limits

The downloaded experiment contains everything needed for `python check.py` and `python plot.py`: run those commands from the extracted directory containing the scripts. To repeat the original-source parity check and full search, clone Wulfic at commit `bf89d3d` and run `python gate.py --source-root ABSOLUTE_CLONE_PATH --check` and `python run.py --source-root ABSOLUTE_CLONE_PATH --check` from the same directory. `snapshot_inputs.py --source-root ABSOLUTE_CLONE_PATH --check` additionally compares the source pages with Liberpedia's `data/pages` files, so run that check in a full Liberpedia checkout. The packaged input snapshot already records the exact Git-object hashes and page text.

This is one grouped replay of the source's **fixed ten keyword assignments and finite F-mask search**. It does not eliminate F as an interruption elsewhere, different mask semantics, other page keys, or a later decoding layer. The standard repeating-key outputs overlap the earlier [prime and keyword streams test](#/experiments/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families); the mask scan and the source's second-layer screens are the additions here.

records.article:
# Keyword decryption, then rearrange the runes

An archived program applies one proposed keyword to each of old pages 21–30 (current **LP2-04–13**), then tries **45 rearrangements per page**. These include prime and Fibonacci position extracts, column routes, reversals, sorting, and whole-word changes. This record replays that specific program; the [other keyword-and-route record](#/experiments/wulfic-keyed-transposition-cohort) tests a different source file.

**Finding:** The strongest source dictionary score on the manuscript is **111**, from reversing the rune order *inside each visible word* on LP2-10. Complete searches on **85 of 199** seeded shuffled versions of the same ten pages reached or exceeded 111. This score does not distinguish that output from the declared shuffle comparison, and no candidate is a validated reading.

![A correctly recovered constructed message scores 1,266 with spaces and zero when the scorer removes word boundaries.](route-summary.svg)

The program's score also cannot rank most of its own routes meaningfully:

- **390 complete rune rearrangements** leave the page's rune counts and normalized coincidence unchanged. Rearrangement can change order, but it cannot by itself improve that frequency statistic.
- **50 whole-word ordering trials** merely rearrange the same decoded words. Their dictionary score is exactly the original score each time.
- **380 character-level outputs** are passed to the source word scorer as one unspaced string. All have word score zero on these ten pages, including the 60 shorter prime/Fibonacci extractions. Those shorter extracts do **not** share the full-page frequency invariant.

For a source-defined positive control, we built a complete **261-rune** wordlist message with the original LP2-04 visible word lengths, reversed it, and encrypted it under that page's assigned keyword. The reverse route recovers every rune exactly. With spaces, the source wordlist gives the message a score of **1,266**; the same recovered runes passed through that route's unspaced scoring path get **zero**. Thus a zero score on a character route cannot exclude a multiword plaintext. This engineered message is intentionally easy for the wordlist and is a scoring control, not a manuscript reading.

The old source labels and page mapping were checked against the current rune transcriptions. The original, unchanged script was run with its committed page and wordlist files staged under its legacy relative paths. The [results](results.json) retain all **450** source route rows and each of the **199** complete shuffled-search maxima. The 199 shuffles are a descriptive, retrospective selection comparison, not a cipher model or a probability that the manuscript is random.

The keyword choices remain proposals. No arbitrary keywords, different word boundaries, alternate source translations or unlisted routes are covered. This replay exposes what the archived program measured; it does not settle whether any rearrangement of LP2 is useful.

## Reproduce

The [plan](plan.json) pins the source revision, each input Git blob, the page mapping, route set and shuffle rule. The upstream program and 3.8 MB wordlist are not redistributed here; obtain the pinned [source revision](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/p21_30_rearrange.py) as a sibling `source-archives/Wulfic-Cicada3301-Liber_Primus` checkout or pass `--source-root` to the runner. The independent checker uses the same pinned Git blobs and reconstructs all 45 routes without calling the source route functions.

```sh
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes/run.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_CHECKOUT --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes/check.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_CHECKOUT
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-rearrangement-routes/plot.py --check
```

The [unaltered source output](source-log.txt) is included as a short execution receipt.

records.article:
# Two running-key searches on LP2-04–13

The archived program tried two ways to use a passage of **Deor** or Emerson's **Self-Reliance** as a key. In one, it applied the passage directly to the page runes. In the other, it combined each passage rune with that page's assigned keyword rune first. It sampled offsets across each key text and tried three ways to combine key and ciphertext values modulo 29.

**Result:** None of the **24,639** source-defined settings passed the program's first screen: the decoded page had to have normalized rune index of coincidence **above 1.3**. The program therefore did not reach its wordlist ranking step on any of these pages. Running the unmodified pinned script on its exact committed inputs printed “No results with IoC > 1.3” for all ten source pages. The ten source rune streams match current LP2-04–13 rune for rune.

![The source gate and controls](gate.svg)

The direct branch checked **12,327** page, offset and mode settings; the keyword-plus-running-key branch checked **12,312**. Their highest normalized coincidence values were **1.148** and **1.173**, below the 1.3 gate. Repeating the full search on **49** seeded shuffles, each of which shuffled every page once and shared that shuffled corpus across all settings, also produced no passing candidate. That control gives no evidence that the gate distinguished the actual pages from these shuffles.

## What the control shows

Nine constructed full-page messages, using the source page's word lengths and the source wordlist, were encrypted and recovered exactly under all three direct modes and six layered modes. All nine cleared the coincidence screen and received positive wordlist scores. The word score ranks passing outputs; it is not a second source acceptance gate. Selecting words from that dictionary also makes these controls unusually easy for its scorer.

After observing the target result, we ran three one-page language checks. The first used **Deor as both message and key**. Its correct setting ranked first, but this shared text makes the check too favorable. The second used Deor as message and Self-Reliance as key. Its intended Deor reading ranked **second**, while the alternative Self-Reliance reading ranked **first**:

```text
cipher = Deor + Self-Reliance  (mod 29)
cipher − Self-Reliance = Deor  (score 68)
cipher − Deor = Self-Reliance  (score 201)
```

For this additive rule, swapping plaintext and key leaves the same ciphertext. Both corpora can therefore produce plausible outputs from one planted cipher, and the higher English score alone cannot identify which text was intended as the key. We kept the rank-two control visible rather than hiding it.

The third check used **261 decoded runes from a documented LP1 reading**, independent of either key text, encrypted with Self-Reliance at offset zero. The complete message was recovered; its coincidence was **1.665**, its source word score **118**, and the correct setting ranked **first** in the same one-page candidate grid. This check shows the source screen can admit one real known-reading sequence under an imposed LP2-04 word skeleton. All three checks were devised **after** the manuscript result, so none is a pre-target estimate of power across other messages or pages.

## Scope and source

The source's old page labels 21–30 mean LP2-04–13 here. The source's data paths were stale after repository relocation; for the exact replay, we staged its **unchanged script and committed file bytes** under the relative paths it expects. The source's two corpora, wordlist, page files and script are each pinned by Git revision and SHA-256 in the [plan](plan.json). Its `range` steps sample roughly **200 direct offsets** and **100 layered offsets** per page and key text, rather than every possible offset. The range also excludes the endpoint where the remaining key text exactly fits the page. The second branch uses only its single assigned keyword per page.

This is a replay of a historical **search rule**, not evidence that running keys or layered keys are impossible. It does not test altered page segmentation, other translations or editions of the key texts, skipped key positions, other keyword assignments, or a decryption that fails the script's coincidence gate. Isolated wordlist matches would not by themselves establish a reading; here, no target candidate reached that stage.

## Reproduce

Use the pinned [source revision](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/p21_30_autokey_solver.py) as a sibling `source-archives/Wulfic-Cicada3301-Liber_Primus` checkout, or pass its path with `--source-root`. The runner verifies every needed Git blob and the ten site-page hashes before comparing any result. This record does not redistribute the upstream corpus or script.

```sh
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-running-key-layers/run.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_CHECKOUT
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-running-key-layers/power.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_CHECKOUT --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-running-key-layers/check.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_CHECKOUT
python experiments/records/wulfic-p21-running-key-layers/plot.py --check
```

The [results](results.json) contain the full grid counts, per-page best records and all 49 null-grid summaries. The [original-script output](source-log.txt) is retained for comparison. The three post-target controls have separate [first](power-addendum.json), [second](power-addendum-v2.json) and [known-reading](power-addendum-v3.json) receipts and plans.

# Prime positions and column order on LP2-07

**Result.** The archived page-24 search's best trigram score was **225**. Running its complete 377-setting search on 256 shuffled versions of the same page produced a score at least that high **222 times**. The selected output does not provide evidence of a reading under this scorer.

![Best trigram scores from the manuscript and 256 full-search shuffled controls](experiments/records/wulfic-page24-prime-columnar/comparison.svg)

The [source scripts](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/p24_prime0_post.py) call this *page 24*. Its pinned rune text matches **LP2-07** here, rune for rune. There are 208 runes. The original scripts point to a page directory that does not exist at that relative path in the pinned repository, so we replayed their stated operations using the pinned page object. We do not treat a missing archived output as a historical negative result.

## What was tried

The [first source script](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/p24_char_tests.py) produces seven views of the page: runes at one-based prime positions, runes at **zero-based** prime positions, the zero-based nonprime complement, and whole-page column readings at widths 5, 7, 11, and 13. A zero-based prime index of 2 picks the **third** rune; a one-based prime position of 2 picks the **second**. Both select 46 runes here. The one-based direct extraction is already included in [Runes at prime and Fibonacci positions](#/experiments/prime-fibonacci-position-extraction); this record adds the source-specific zero-based and columnar steps.

The second source script takes only the 46 zero-based-prime runes. It lays them in rows of width **2 through 14**, reads down columns, then subtracts each shift **0 through 28** modulo 29. That is **13 × 29 = 377 settings** in one search. Its fixed scorer joins the rune names into Latin letters and sums a short list of weighted three-letter fragments. The highest score came from width **10**, shift **16**. The [full result file](experiments/records/wulfic-page24-prime-columnar/results.json) preserves every score and output hash.

The source also prints index of coincidence (IoC), but it cannot rank these 377 settings: column reading only rearranges the same 46 runes, and a uniform shift relabels them. Every setting therefore has exactly the same GP29 IoC, **0.981**. The four whole-page column readings likewise all have the page's IoC, **1.043**. Their output streams are recorded as observations; the source specifies no separate pass rule for them.

## How to read the comparison

Each control shuffled all 208 runes within LP2-07, then repeated the **whole 377-setting selection**. The observed maximum's add-one comparison is **223/257 ≈ 0.868**. A synthetic page with a repeated THE pattern planted at the zero-based prime positions passed the exact selector, column reading, shift, and source trigram scorer; its best full-search score exceeded 49 synthetic random-page controls. This checks the implementation and a favorable pattern, not whether the short source scorer recognizes real prose reliably.

This is a bounded test of a **46-rune selection on one page**. It does not exclude another index origin, a further cipher layer, different page boundaries, or a different language model. A few weighted fragments in a selected short string would not establish a decryption.

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-page24-prime-columnar/plan.json) fixes the operations and controls. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-page24-prime-columnar/check.py` for an independent reconstruction of every setting and shuffle, or `python experiments/records/wulfic-page24-prime-columnar/run.py --check` to repeat the saved result.

records.article:
# Does rune equality reveal a repeating alphabet?

If an encryption alphabet repeats every **L** runes, the same alphabet acts on positions `i` and `i+L`. A one-to-one alphabet preserves whether those two plaintext runes are equal. Wulfic's Stage AE uses that invariant to check **every possible lag from 11 to 12,945** in the joined unsolved LP2 text. This is a way to test a whole family of periodic substitutions without guessing the alphabets themselves.

**Result:** the source's controlled rule excludes **10,030 of 12,935 periods**, including 1033, 1729 and 3301. It leaves **2,905 periods open**. No period has the excess equality required for a positive detection. An open period is not evidence that it is the key length.

![Observed LP2 rune equality versus the lowest planted periodic-alphabet rate at periods 1033, 1729 and 3301](experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags/comparison.svg)

| Repeating period | LP2 equal rune pairs | LP2 rate | Lowest planted-control rate | Source verdict |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1033 | 422 / 11,923 | 3.54% | 5.65% | Excluded |
| 1729 | 407 / 11,227 | 3.63% | 5.20% | Excluded |
| 3301 | 326 / 9,655 | 3.38% | 5.69% | Excluded |

The figure shows *rates* for three named periods. The actual decision uses a binomial tail, not a simple line at 5%. The [complete source table](experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags/source-stage_ae_lags.tsv) has the pair count, equality count, rates and verdict for every tested lag.

## What the comparison means

The source assumes a periodic key selecting a fixed, **bijective** rune alphabet at each residue position. At the correct period, equal ciphertext pairs then occur exactly where plaintext pairs are equal, before any other processing. The model allows the observed anti-doublet tendency by redrawing 81% of adjacent repeat collisions in its simulated streams. Its lower-bound test asks whether the observed equality count is unusually small if the plaintext's agreement probability is at least 5%.

The source generated 20 flat-rune null streams and 100 periodic-alphabet positive controls: ten each from Emerson prose and solved LP1 at periods 1033, 1729, 3301, 6000 and 9000. None of the 20 null streams triggered its positive rule. **All 100 positive controls passed and none was excluded** at its planted period. The full source run reported valid. This establishes that its chosen controls can distinguish these planted cases; it does not prove that every natural-language text or every periodic cipher has the same agreement rate.

The exclusion count is conditional on the source's English/LP1 control sources, 5% minimum-agreement assumption, binomial model and archived transcription. Lag pairs share rune positions, so the binomial tail is a model-based score rather than an exact independent-trial probability. The per-lag exclusion threshold is not a correction for selecting among all 12,935 periods. A changing alphabet, non-bijective mapping, running state, word reset or additional transformation may break the equality invariant. These cases remain outside the test.

## Reproduce

The two bundled tables were regenerated from the unmodified [pinned Stage AE program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_ae.py) at commit `bf89d3d`; both match that revision's output byte-for-byte. From the extracted Liberpedia repository, Python's standard library verifies the bundle and independently recounts all 12,935 lag agreements from the 56 page text files:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags/check.py
python experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags/plot.py --check
```

The independent checker builds a bitset for each rune, counts matches at every lag, verifies the three named lower-tail probabilities, and checks a planted periodic alphabet that must preserve equality. The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-alphabet-lags/plan.json) pins all manuscript inputs and source revision. The optional `replay_source.py` reruns the original program from a matching checkout; it requires that repository and its NumPy dependency. Wulfic's Stages AC and AD explore related lagged-key ideas, but their pinned `--quick` runs fail in a shared control-array shape operation before LP2 scoring. This record does not present their historical outputs as reproduced.

records.article:
# Can word cribs predict a periodic key?

The archived solver tries familiar words at each visible word slot, converts each guess into votes for a repeating key, and chooses the most-voted value at each key position. We replayed its two stated examples: archived `page_30` with period 17 and `page_27` with period 43. Those files are **LP2-13** and **LP2-10** in the current reader; their rune text matches exactly.

## The check that matters

We inferred a key from half the visible word slots, then read the untouched half. Across both pages, both folds and all three source directions, **none of the untouched words exactly matches an encoded source-dictionary word**. The source's full-stream vocabulary scores are 10–19, but those count substrings anywhere in the joined rune text. They are not 10–19 independently recovered words.

![The key voted from half the word slots predicts no exact dictionary words in the untouched half, and known-message controls fail.](experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-word-crib-votes/heldout.svg)

The stronger caution is the **known-message control**. We encrypted source-dictionary words with a planted period-17 or period-43 key and applied the same vote and holdout procedure. The best fold recovered 11 of 31 untouched eligible words; several recovered none. All 12 planted folds miss the predeclared 50% recovery requirement. Thus this particular vote heuristic is not validated as a detector. Its failure on LP2 cannot exclude periodic keys.

## What the source actually tests

The implementation checks whether each proposed word gives a consistent key **within that word**. It then tallies votes for each key residue independently. Although its description promises consistency with *other* word slots, the code does not require a complete mutually consistent sentence or key. The source's three directions also include equivalent subtraction/addition reconstructions under signed keys; those are alternate parameterizations, not independent confirmations.

The dictionary has 335 source entries, 309 distinct GP rune words after encoding. The page and period pairs were examples in the script, not periods established by this experiment. A 199-shuffle whole-selection reference was computed across both pages, all three directions and both folds, but **its rank is not interpreted** because the positive control failed. This record measures the specified solver, not the entire periodic-key family.

Four related source scripts validate candidate phrases against `data/gpu_hill_checkpoint_gpu1.json`; that checkpoint is absent from the pinned public tree. We have not replaced it with another key or described those validations as reproduced. The separate `lp_crib_drag.py` uses a different linked-position rule and is outside this record.

## Repeat it

From a clone of [the pinned source revision](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/tree/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c), run `python experiments/records/wulfic-periodic-word-crib-votes/run.py --source-root PATH_TO_CLONE --check` to recalculate all saved rows and controls. The independent `check.py --source-root PATH_TO_CLONE` extracts the original dictionary directly from the source, reconstructs the six unrefined keys and twelve holdout scores, and checks the source stdout receipts. Omit `--check` to regenerate the saved outputs.

# How many independent key alphabets would LP2 need?

If each key value selects its own **unrelated, randomly chosen rune alphabet**, repeatedly using only a few key values should leave a measurable bias in the ciphertext. Wulfic's Stage T asks how many effectively distinct key values that model needs before LP2's nearly even rune counts cease to be surprising. “Effective” accounts for uneven key frequencies: 29 equally used values give 29 effective classes; a key dominated by a few values has fewer.

**Finding:** under the source's declared 1-in-10,000 lower-tail rule, the model is excluded through **168 effective key classes** if one set of alphabets serves the joined LP2 text. If each of eight marked sections gets a fresh set, the source's bound is **174**. Larger class counts are **not excluded**, which is not evidence that they decrypt anything. This is a bound on one kind of random substitution scheme, not an identified cipher or a reading.

![Two conditional effective-class bounds, 168 and 174](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound/comparison.svg)

The joined test uses all **12,956 runes** on LP2-00–55. The sectioned test uses **12,947**: source sections 7–9 and 11–15, omitting a nine-rune section at the start of LP2-15 as its rule specifies. These are [marked sections of the pinned transcription](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/data/canonical/liber_primus_master.txt), not necessarily whole pages. The independent checker reconstructed them from Liberpedia's page text and reproduced the source's pooled chi-square **26.36** and eight-section sum **194.14**.

## What was tested

The model gives each key value a separate random permutation of the 29-rune alphabet. A fixed value always uses its assigned permutation. The test measures the overall rune counts, without selecting a key phase or fitting plaintext words. The [source program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_t.py) calibrated the model using the rune distribution of solved LP1 text. Before inspecting the manuscript statistic, its declared gates passed on **200 generated ciphers** each at 29, 256 and 1,024 classes. At 1,024 classes, **0 of 200** controls were falsely excluded at the strict threshold.

The source also evaluated **20 specified key-class schemes**. Fifteen fell below the conditional bound, including prime values reduced modulo 29 and the source's byte streams reduced modulo 29. Five raw-byte classings, with roughly 236–255 effective classes, were not excluded. That says only that this frequency test lacks the power to reject them. It does not validate those byte files as puzzle keys. See the [complete source table](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound/source-stage_t_results.tsv) for each classing and its effective count.

The source reports a stricter **153/133** pair after scaling the observations by a factor learned from an additive control. This was a **post-run sensitivity check**, not the declared rule that produced 168/174. An additive or Vigenère-style *Latin-square* alphabet can look flat even with few key classes; Stage T does not reject that family. It also does not cover correlated or deliberately balanced substitution alphabets, transposition, or additional layers.

## Reproduce

From the Liberpedia repository root, these standard-library checks verify the source table hash, the control decisions, independent LP2 rune counts and statistics, the analytic pooled boundary, and the figure:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound/plot.py --check
```

The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound/plan.json) pins the source revision and rules. For a complete Monte Carlo replay, including the **2,000,000-draw** sectioned reference, run the optional wrapper with a matching external checkout and NumPy:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound/replay_source.py PATH_TO_WULFIC_CLONE
```

It runs the unchanged source program into a temporary file. Its **45 output rows match the pinned published results byte-for-byte**. The independent bundled check verifies the manuscript statistics and pooled analytic boundary; the sectioned Monte Carlo bound is verified by that full source replay.

# Could earlier Cicada bytes select LP2's substitution alphabet?

One proposed way to use another file as a key is to let **each byte select a hidden rune alphabet**. The same byte selects the same alphabet whenever it returns. Wulfic's Stage W tests that model without guessing the alphabets: it asks whether runes under a repeated byte label show the repetitions expected of text. It checks five specified byte streams at every source phase, once for each of nine marked sections and once across the joined text of **LP2-00–55**.

**Finding:** the source's control gate passes. None of its **50 key/alignment settings** reaches the +30-nat detection threshold. **Twelve** have enough positive-control power to exclude this exact model; **38** are untestable, so their low LP2 scores do not count as exclusions. The best LP2 score is **+0.84**, using source byte file `page_17.bin` against the section covering **LP2-23–26**; that setting is untestable. No reading is produced.

![Stage W decisions for five key sources, ten alignments per source](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/comparison.svg)

The figure's “Page 17/21/43” labels name [byte files in the source repository](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/tree/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/data/outguess), **not** manuscript pages LP2-17/21/43. Their origin as puzzle payloads has not been independently verified here. The marked sections follow the [`$` boundaries in the source transcription](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/data/canonical/liber_primus_master.txt). We checked its rune sequence against Liberpedia's page text: all **56** LP2 pages match rune for rune. Relevant boundaries are: section 11, the last 150 runes of LP2-15 through LP2-22; section 12, LP2-23–26; and section 15, LP2-40–55. Section 10 contains only the first nine runes of LP2-15, so these sections are not always whole-page ranges.

| Source byte stream | Excluded alignments | Untestable |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Wisdom hint | Joined LP2-00–55; LP2-40–55 | 8 |
| Wisdom hint, reversed | Joined LP2-00–55; LP2-40–55 | 8 |
| Source file `page_17.bin` | Joined LP2-00–55; LP2-40–55 | 8 |
| Source file `page_21.bin` | Joined LP2-00–55; LP2-15 (after first nine runes)–22; LP2-40–55 | 7 |
| Source file `page_43.bin` | Joined LP2-00–55; LP2-15 (after first nine runes)–22; LP2-40–55 | 7 |

These are **five source keys under one method**, evaluated at ten alignments. They are not fifty unrelated solving ideas. The [complete candidate table](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/source-stage_w_candidates.tsv) gives every score, phase and verdict.

## Why the controls matter

The score uses rune repetitions within each byte-selected class. It averages a likelihood ratio over **all possible starting phases** of the named byte key; the best individual phase is shown separately in the table, but it is **not** the decision score. The source regards a mean score of at least **+30 nats** as a hit.

For each key and alignment, Stage W makes five synthetic messages encrypted by that exact kind of byte-selected alphabet and five flat negative messages made with an unrelated additive key. It also scores one LP2 stream against each shuffled key. If any flat negative or shuffled-key null reaches +30, the whole run is void. The highest such negative here is **+0.64**. A specific key/alignment is called excluded only if **all five** same-length positives reach +30 while LP2 does not. This is why the many short sections remain untestable, even though their LP2 scores are low. The [control table](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/source-stage_w_controls.tsv) shows all **505** controls.

The earlier Stage S used the same LP2 score but its original negative-control design made that run void. We regenerated just the **50 Stage S LP2 scores** that Stage W requires. Each row matches the corresponding row in the pinned source's full 200-row Stage S table, and all 50 agree with the Stage W candidates. This numerical dependency does **not** revive Stage S's invalid conclusion; Stage W's own corrected controls decide what can be said here.

The result applies to these raw byte streams, their source-defined phase search and a key that stays in step. Skips, resets, another key source, a changing alphabet or an additional cipher layer are outside the tested model.

## Reproduce

From the Liberpedia repository root, Python's standard library checks the three bundled tables, recalculates all source verdicts and verifies the figure:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/plot.py --check
```

The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/plan.json) pins the source revision, byte-file hashes, all settings and the decision rules. The two Stage W tables were regenerated with the unmodified [pinned Stage W program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_w.py) and match its published source files **byte-for-byte**. The Stage S subset was regenerated with the [pinned score function](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_s.py). To repeat the full calculation from a matching external checkout with NumPy:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-position-alphabet-long-keys/replay_source.py PATH_TO_WULFIC_CLONE
```

That wrapper verifies the pinned inputs, regenerates the Stage S dependency and the two Stage W tables in a temporary directory, then compares them byte-for-byte with the bundled files. The source code remains in its original repository.

record_type.description: Reconstructs a supplied proposed method and its choices; reproduction is not independent confirmation of a reading.

The prime-stream search tested 11,880 settings and yielded nine permissive sequential screen hits; its highest IoC was 1.174 on LP2-09 (1/49 shuffles reached it), but that output missed all six one-rune checks and did not read as a passage. records.article:
# Prime and keyword streams in three archived searches

Could a familiar word, a reordered prime list, or a word-controlled walk through primes decode these LP2 pages? Three archived scripts ask related questions. We replayed their complete finite grids together on verified page text. **The source screens do not establish a complete reading.** One prime-stream IoC peak is unusual against this small control set, so it remains a lead to inspect rather than a solved page.

![Observed maximum IoC for each source search against 49 complete shuffled searches](experiments/records/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families/comparison.svg)

| Source method | What it tried | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repeating keywords | 18 named words, three directions, ten pages | None of 540 outputs made every one-rune word an I or A. The best IoC was 1.119, reached or exceeded in 18 of 49 shuffled searches. |
| Prime streams | Sequential and five alternate prime orders; three key forms, three directions, and the source's F-skip rule on eight pages | Nine sequential settings passed at least one permissive source screen. The highest IoC was 1.174 on LP2-09; one of 49 shuffled searches reached it. This output missed all six one-rune word checks and its inspected opening is not a coherent passage. |
| Keyword-stepped primes | 20 literal keyword arrays, eight prime-index rules, offsets 0–1000, three directions, eleven pages | Of 5,285,280 settings, 2,270 passed the source's all-singleton I/A gate. None reached its IoC > 1.3 hit threshold. The highest gated IoC was 1.281; 12 of 49 shuffled searches reached it. |

These are **three source methods**, not millions of separate experiments. The control repeats each entire search after shuffling rune order *within each page*, so the comparison includes the choice of its best setting. A shuffled page preserves length and rune frequencies, but not word structure or a realistic encryption process. Forty-nine controls give only a coarse reference, especially for a rare peak. An IoC peak or a short accidental word is not a decryption.

## What was actually replayed

The archived programs call pages `page_21`, `page_28`, and so forth. Those map to current **LP2-04** and **LP2-11** by subtracting 17; the archive's page bytes and rune counts were checked against the current page text before scoring. The source's word-boundary parsers differ slightly, so each branch keeps its own one-rune positions. The programs' relocated file paths are broken in the archived checkout; this replay uses the verified pinned input bytes and preserves the source operations and scoring screens.

The first script repeats 18 parsed keywords. Its optional `data/verified_keys.json` branch was left out: that exact path is absent from the pinned Git tree. An archived file with the same basename exists elsewhere in the tree, but the script does not load it and its provenance was not assumed. The prime script uses 80 valid sequential offsets plus five named nonsequential generators; its listed offset 5000 cannot hold a page in the source's 5,133-prime table. Its `gp_ext` stream repeats sequential offset zero, so it is an output alias. The stepped script searches all 20 literal arrays and all eight source generators. Some `keyword_add_sequential` settings already occur in the earlier [combined keyword-and-prime test](#/experiments/wulfic-keyword-prime-layer-grid): 17,600 source settings share those exact arrays, offsets, signs, and pages. That overlap is recorded, not counted as a new idea.

The highest prime IoC comes from adding a totient-based sequential stream starting at prime index 110 on LP2-09. Its IoC is 1.174, quick word score is 9, and **zero of six** source one-rune word positions become I or A. The script's top *retained* candidate is different because it ranks permissive screen hits by a combined heuristic. Neither output is a documented reading. Further work would need a fixed rule that predicts a longer passage or an untouched page, not a higher score selected from another flexible grid.

## Check and reproduce

Each branch passed a synthetic arithmetic control: a planted GP29 stream with I/A at all one-rune positions was encrypted under one declared setting, then recovered exactly and crossed the source hit threshold. This checks that the operations can detect that artificial pattern; it does not establish power to recognize English. We also compared sampled key streams, decodes, and keyword parsing with functions extracted from the pinned source revision. An independent scalar checker reconstructs every saved page winner and its full decoded-output hash.

The [result table](experiments/records/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families/results.json), [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families/plan.json), and [input snapshot](experiments/records/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families/inputs.json) specify the exact pages, keys, counts, null seed, and source revision. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families/check.py` for the independent checks. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-prime-keyword-stream-families/run.py --check` to repeat all three complete grids and 49 controls. The optional `source_parity.py` additionally requires a checkout of the pinned upstream commit.

This bounded replay covers those exact old source settings and selected LP2 pages. It does not exclude different keywords, prime orderings, resets, pages, or cipher families.

scope.procedure: Run pinned Stage U's G1 model calibration, G2 flat-key power and G3 same-family false-exclusion checks, then score all 24 LP2 settings. Independently rebuild both manuscript chi-square statistics and audit each source verdict.

records.article:
# Do random Quagmire alphabets fit LP2's rune frequencies?

A Quagmire-style cipher can relabel plaintext runes, add a key value modulo 29, then relabel the output again. Wulfic's Stage U asks a limited question about that family: **if those relabellings are random**, would the resulting ciphertext usually have rune counts as even as LP2's?

**Finding:** the source's simulation gates pass. Of **24 declared settings**, **20 are excluded** at its strict frequency threshold. The other **four**, all using a uniformly chosen letter from A–Z as the key value, lack enough positive-control power and are **untestable** under the source rule. None is a decryption, and an untestable setting is not support for its cipher.

![Six Quagmire key-value families with twenty excluded and four untestable settings](experiments/records/wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets/comparison.svg)

The source fixes **six key-value distributions**: English rune values, their prime values, English Latin-letter frequencies, uniformly chosen decimal digits, uniformly chosen hex digits, and uniformly chosen A–Z letters. Each is checked with an independent key alphabet or one tied to the plaintext alphabet. Each of those is checked on the joined **12,956 LP2 runes** and on eight marked sections with fresh alphabets, for **6 × 2 × 2 = 24** settings. The sectioned statistic leaves out the nine-rune header section on LP2-15, as declared in the [source program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_u.py).

## What an exclusion means

For each setting, the source draws **100,000 random alphabet combinations** and asks how often their expected bias would permit LP2's low chi-square value. It requires the probability to be at most **0.0001** both before and after its declared anti-doublet adjustment. It first checks the simulation against known generated ciphers. All six model checks passed; none of the **20 same-family controls per setting** was falsely excluded. A setting can be called excluded only if the rule also rejects at least **18 of 20** flat-key controls. The four A–Z settings fail that power requirement. The [complete 80-row result table](experiments/records/wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets/source-stage_u_results.tsv) retains every gate and setting.

This result is narrower than “Quagmire was tried.” It uses only overall rune counts and six specified key-value distributions. It says nothing about exact key order, a deterministic keyword alphabet, a different key distribution, another segmentation, or a second cipher layer. Stage T's [independent-random-alphabet bound](#/experiments/wulfic-position-alphabet-flatness-bound) concerns a different model; its warning that a flat *Latin-square* key can escape that bound remains valid. Stage U tests particular Quagmire mixtures with their own controls rather than inheriting Stage T's exclusion.

## Reproduce

The standard-library checker reads Liberpedia's page runes independently, confirms the two manuscript chi-square statistics, and checks all **24** source control/decision rows:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets/plot.py --check
```

The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets/plan.json) fixes the source revision and simulation rules. To rerun the entire pinned source calculation with NumPy, use:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-quagmire-random-alphabets/replay_source.py PATH_TO_WULFIC_CLONE
```

We ran the unchanged program and compared its generated table with the [pinned source result](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/reference/findings/stage_u_results.tsv): all **80 rows match byte-for-byte**. The optional wrapper regenerates the table in a temporary file. The full run takes substantially longer than the bundled checks.

records.article:
# An alphabet that turns at runes and separators

An archived solver tried a changing alphabet with two clocks: one shift after each rune and another after a word or other visible separator. **None of its eleven LP2 targets passes its own frequency gate**, whether we preserve its literal rune parser or correct a glyph omission. This is a bounded result for the source's specified shifts and target pages; it is not a test of every Alberti disk or changing alphabet.

![Each LP2 page's highest collision score under the two-clock grid remains below the source's 1.4 hit gate.](experiments/records/wulfic-separator-clock-alberti/comparison.svg)

The chart shows the largest **normalized index of coincidence** (a measure of repeated rune values) after trying every source clock setting on each page. The source calls a result a hit only above **1.4**. Its best LP2 value is **1.164** with the original parser and **1.159** when the missing rune is restored. There are **zero gated outputs** on either representation. The source also listed old page 15, which is actually solved **LP1-15**; its literal parser produced two gate-passing settings there. That solved page is displayed in the [result table](experiments/records/wulfic-separator-clock-alberti/results.json) but excluded from the LP2 comparison.

## What was tested

At position `i`, the alphabet has turned by `letter_shift × i + separator_shift × separators_before_i` modulo 29. The source tries every shift from **0 to 28**, both directions and three decode modes. That is **5,046 named settings** per page, but they collapse to **1,682 distinct outputs**: opposite directions and arithmetic signs often describe the same transformation. We retained the source's page list, zero starting phase, separator rule, IoC gate, and bigram/trigram ranking above that gate. The selected old source page ordinals map to the LP2 pages labeled in the chart.

The original program lists `ᛂ` where the archived manuscript uses `ᛄ`. As a result, its literal parser drops **5–13 runes** from each named LP2 page. We show that exact parser and a separately declared canonical-GP correction. The correction is a *new input variant*, not a reconstruction of a historical run. A second source issue is path placement: the archived script changes into `tools/` and then looks for a `pages/` directory there. Our replay reads the exact pinned Git page files instead. These old files match the site's archived rune sequence before applying the source parser.

## How strong is the result?

Before testing LP2, we used four archived known readings to make **eight planted messages**, one under each parser per reading. A chosen two-clock schedule recovered all eight exactly, and all eight cleared the source's 1.4 gate. We also compared 24 cases directly with the pinned source decoder. The independent checker reconstructed every observed page and all **49 complete-search shuffled controls**. None of those shuffled controls cleared the gate either. That control has too few positive hits to assign a useful tail probability to the LP2 zero; it does show that merely searching many clocks does not force a hit under this threshold.

The outcome is limited to the eleven source-selected LP2 pages, these two parsers, the page-local two-clock rule, and the source's gate. Adding a constant starting phase only renames the output symbols, so it cannot change IoC or make this gate pass. Other separator meanings, alphabets, plaintext languages, and extra cipher layers remain open. A readable passage or an independently predicted held-out page would be needed to support a new clock rule.

## Reproduce

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-separator-clock-alberti/plan.json), [source-page snapshot](experiments/records/wulfic-separator-clock-alberti/inputs.json), [gate receipt](experiments/records/wulfic-separator-clock-alberti/gate_results.json), and [results](experiments/records/wulfic-separator-clock-alberti/results.json) carry the exact bytes and case counts. In the extracted experiment folder, `python check.py` independently repeats the page and control censuses; `python plot.py` regenerates the chart. To repeat source parity, use `python gate.py --source-root ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_PINNED_WULFIC_CLONE`. To repeat all computations after the gate, run `python run.py --check`. To regenerate the input snapshot, run `python snapshot_inputs.py --source-root ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_PINNED_WULFIC_CLONE --liberpedia-root ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_LIBERPEDIA_CHECKOUT`.

records.article:
# Do these pages reveal a repeating key length?

Two checks in Wulfic's archived [session 17 program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/session17_clean_solve.py) look for a repeating key period. They **both detected a planted period of 13**, but neither gives convincing evidence for a period in the tested LP2 pages.

![The known-plaintext lag check found no LP2 result above its report line. The split-column check flagged about as many LP2 pages as a typical complete shuffled search.](experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/comparison.svg)

**Check 8** tries eight fixed passages as possible plaintext on **LP2-04–17**. At each sampled alignment, it asks: “If this were the plaintext, would the implied key repeat after a prime number of runes?” The strongest LP2 match repeated at **10 of 76 positions**—**13.2%**, below the source's **greater than 25%** report rule. None of the **4,239 distinct passage/alignment searches** crossed that rule. Twelve of 49 complete shuffled searches reached at least the observed best fraction. The source calculates both subtraction and addition implied keys, but one is the negative of the other, so their equality-at-a-lag evidence is identical; these are **8,478 source settings, not 8,478 independent ideas**.

**Check 9** needs no guessed plaintext. On **LP2-04–37**, it splits each page into columns according to candidate prime periods, then compares the columns' rune repetition with the whole page. Its stated line flagged **29 of 34 pages**. That looks broad until the same complete scan is repeated after shuffling every page: the middle of 49 shuffled searches also flags **29 pages**, and **26 of 49** flag at least as many. The largest single LP2 column-to-page ratio was **2.28**; **5 of 49** shuffled whole scans reached it. The source also lists factors of distances between repeated trigrams, but sets no acceptance threshold for those factors, so they are preserved as descriptive data, not treated as separate hits.

The planted control used the source's own P03 candidate text and a fixed 13-value repeating key. Check 8 ranked that exact period and text alignment first, with **248 of 248** lag pairs equal. Check 9 flagged period 13 on the planted page. Yet Check 9 also flagged **27 of 34** seeded uniform control pages, showing that its 1.3× page-baseline line is permissive in this grid. The plant tests whether these detectors can register a clean periodic construction; it does not calibrate every language, page length or interrupted cipher.

The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/plan.json) pins the exact source passages, offsets, prime periods, page mapping, thresholds and 49 shared full-search shuffles. [Results](experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/results.json) retain all page/period values, the complete known-plaintext reports, Kasiski summaries and each shuffled maximum. The [control result](experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/control-results.json) was written before checking LP2. The old source page numbers **21–54** map to the site's **LP2-04–37**; all 34 pinned rune streams match the site rune for rune.

We also ran the unchanged pinned source script with its exact page files in a temporary directory. Its Test 8 printed **no strong periodicity**, and its Test 9 marked exactly the same **29 pages**. The [source execution receipt](experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/source-replay.json) hashes the complete stdout after normalizing line endings to LF. This matches the source's printed verdicts; our saved tables make its underlying measurements and full-search controls inspectable.

These are period *screens*, not decryption tests. Check 8's authored passages could differ from any intended text, and its sampled alignments can miss an untried alignment. Check 9's highest ratios often occur at long periods with short residue columns. The 49 shuffles preserve each page's rune counts but do not model an encryption algorithm; the fractions above are descriptive full-selection comparisons, not universal probabilities. Other periods, boundaries, transcriptions, layers and changing key clocks remain outside scope. A separate [LP2-31 test](#/experiments/lp2-31-periodic-ioc) used one page, periods 2–20 and a different pooled coincidence statistic.

To reproduce, supply a separate Git checkout containing the pinned Wulfic revision; its unlicensed source is not copied into the experiment bundle:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/run.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_WULFIC_CHECKOUT --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/check.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_WULFIC_CHECKOUT
python experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/replay_source.py --source-root PATH_TO_PINNED_WULFIC_CHECKOUT --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-session17-period-detectors/plot.py --check
```

The runner verifies exact source and page bytes. Its independent checker counts matching modular differences at each lag directly and enumerates equal rune pairs within split columns, then repeats the complete planted and shuffled searches without importing the runner.
records.reader_finding: The known-text lag screen found no source-defined hit. The split-column screen flagged many pages, but it flagged about as many after shuffling; both could detect a clean planted period.
records.reader_limit: Only source passages, sampled offsets, named pages and prime periods were checked. A flagged period is not a decipherment.

# Does the LP2-15 number square decode its short heading?

The [LP2-15](#/reader/lp2-15) heading has **two words, four and five runes long**, followed by a 4×4 number square. Wulfic's Stage I asks a narrow question: if the square's construction supplies a nine-number key, can a fixed arithmetic operation turn the **whole heading** into two words in a declared vocabulary?

**Finding:** none of the **30 complete outputs** passes that two-word test. This closes the tested combination of five square-derived number sequences, two reading directions and three arithmetic rules. It does **not** rule out other routes through the square, another spelling convention, or a cipher on the body text.

![The LP2-15 heading tested under five keys, two directions and three operations](experiments/records/wulfic-square-title-vocabulary/comparison.svg)

The five sequences are the printed cell values in the source's spiral order, Fibonacci-indexed primes, those primes minus one, their one-based Fibonacci indices, and the Fibonacci indices themselves. Each is read outward or inward. The first nine values, reduced modulo 29, are applied as ciphertext minus key, ciphertext plus key, or key minus ciphertext. The original **4 + 5 word boundary** stays fixed. The [source-defined vocabulary](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_i.py) uses the solved translation and four pinned English texts, converted to GP rune spellings.

The source also tried **20,000** seeded random nine-rune subtraction keys against the same two-word gate and observed **zero** passes. That is an empirical control, not a zero probability: the vocabulary is a deliberately strict screen, and it cannot by itself decide whether a decoded phrase is meaningful. The [full 30-line source output](experiments/records/wulfic-square-title-vocabulary/source-title-output.txt) shows every complete candidate without selecting attractive fragments.

## Reproduce

The bundled standard-library check independently reads Liberpedia's LP2-15 rune text, reconstructs the Fibonacci and prime sequences, verifies that the sixteen calculated cell values match the printed square's set, and recalculates all **30** outputs:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-square-title-vocabulary/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-square-title-vocabulary/plot.py --check
```

The vocabulary decisions and 20,000-key control come from the pinned source. Recompute them from its original translation and corpora, without copying those texts into Liberpedia:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-square-title-vocabulary/replay_source.py PATH_TO_WULFIC_CLONE
```

The wrapper checks the source revision and input hashes, then compares the source output **byte-for-byte**. The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-square-title-vocabulary/plan.json) records the exact bounds and exclusions.

# Do page and line starts reset an alphabet?

**This particular restart model does not match the unsolved manuscript.** At a fixed position after each restart, the model uses the same substitution alphabet every time. A repeated plaintext rune at that position should therefore produce a repeated ciphertext rune. The five proposed restart points—section, paragraph, clause, line and page—were all checked. LP2's same-position repeats stayed close to a random-rune baseline and below the conservative range of planted examples.

![Five restart-boundary comparisons: LP2 near the random-rune expectation, planted examples higher.](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/comparison.svg)

The blue bars are LP2. The gray bars begin at the **lower bound** of simulated manuscripts deliberately encrypted with an alphabet that restarts at the named boundary. Ratios use a separate random-rune expectation for each boundary, so a value of 1 means “about as many matches as random output.” The bars do not represent decoded text.

## What was tested

This is a replay of [Wulfic's Stage AB source program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_ab.py), not a new proposed decryption. It takes all **12,956 runes on the 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages**. For each boundary type, it groups runes by their position from the start of that unit. It then counts pairs of units that carry the same ciphertext rune at the same position. Words that wrap across a line or page do not create a new clause or paragraph.

The original run compared each count with **1,000 random-rune controls** using the source's measured anti-doublet rule, then tested detection power with **200 planted restart encryptions from each of two plaintext sources**: Emerson essays and known LP readings. The source's lower bound is five standard deviations below the mean of log(count + 1), transformed back to counts. The frozen inputs, random seed **3301**, threshold and source revision are in the [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/plan.json).

| Restart point | LP2 matches | Random mean | Weaker planted lower bound |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Section | 1,125 | 1,145 | 1,755 |
| Paragraph | 1,484 | 1,525 | 2,365 |
| Clause | 20,028 | 19,874 | 32,271 |
| Line | 126,508 | 125,457 | 203,912 |
| Page | 10,751 | 10,726 | 17,307 |

For all five rows, even the lowest of the planted control results is above the highest random control. LP2 is below the planted lower bound in both plaintext sources. The source therefore marks each row **excluded within this model**. Our full run reproduced the upstream [result table](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/source-stage_ab_results.tsv) and [control table](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/source-stage_ab_controls.tsv) byte-for-byte.

The finding does **not** reject every cipher that restarts on a page or line. It concerns a shared, position-dependent substitution alphabet, the source's plaintext examples and its post-encryption anti-doublet process. A changing key, feedback, distinct alphabet at each unit, different plaintext distribution or another preprocessing rule can break this invariant. It also does not tell us what cipher LP2 uses.

## Reproduce

Download this experiment and run `python experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/run.py --check`, then `python experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/check.py`. The [independent checker](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/check.py) rebuilds the complete rune stream and all five boundary partitions from Liberpedia's page JSON, matches the [frozen source-derived layout](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/layout.json), and recalculates the observed statistic and analytic random expectation. It also checks a planted, fixed-position substitution example.

To rerun all 1,000 null and 2 × 200 planted trials under the **original source code**, clone the [source repository](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus), check out commit `bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c`, install NumPy and run `python experiments/records/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets/replay_source.py --source-dir PATH_TO_CLONE`. The wrapper verifies the source revision and input hashes, writes into a temporary directory, and requires byte-identical output tables. The manuscript is not reinterpreted or rescored in that replay.
