records.article:
# Could a restarted key also shift at every boundary?

**The tested shifted-restart model still does not fit LP2.** Giving each page, line or other unit its own additive shift removes the simple rune-for-rune comparison used in the [basic restart test](#/experiments/wulfic-stage-ab-reset-alphabets). It does not remove a second property: subtract two ciphertext runes *within the same unit*, and that unit's shift cancels. If the underlying position key restarts, equal plaintext differences at the same two positions still produce equal ciphertext differences across units.

![Five shifted-restart comparisons: LP2 near the random expectation, planted controls to the right.](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/comparison.svg)

Each blue point is LP2's full difference-match count divided by the random-rune expectation for that boundary. Gray is the conservative lower bound from planted shifted-restart encryptions. **The horizontal scale is zoomed from 0.98 to 1.08** to make the modest but consistent separation visible; it does not start at zero. None of these points is decoded text.

## What was tested

This is a byte-for-byte replay of [Wulfic's Stage AF program](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/run_stage_af.py) at its pinned revision. The model uses one shared key value at each position after a restart and one extra shift for each unit. It covers both additive and Beaufort directions in planted controls. For every section, paragraph, clause, line and page boundary, the statistic compares ciphertext differences between positions **2–300 runes apart within that same unit**. The complete input is **12,956 runes across 55 rune-bearing LP2 pages**.

The source tested **200 flat-rune nulls** and **100 planted encryptions for each of two plaintext sources**, Emerson essays and solved LP readings. Its anti-doublet rule was applied to controls. A test could be called excluded only where both planted sources separated from the null and LP2 fell below both predeclared five-standard-deviation lower bounds. The frozen [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/plan.json) records the exact rule and source hashes.

The page-reset case is illustrative: LP2 had **1,207,810** matching within-page differences; random controls averaged **1,208,036**. The weaker planted lower bound was **1,242,113**. The same comparison held at the other four boundaries, so the source marks all five cells **excluded under this model**. Our full source run reproduced its [results](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/source-stage_af_results.tsv) and [controls](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/source-stage_af_controls.tsv) byte-for-byte.

This does not rule out every resetting key. It tests a **shared position key plus one constant shift per unit**, using the source's plaintext examples and doublet treatment. Position-dependent shifts inside a unit, nonlinear feedback, a different plaintext distribution or a different boundary rule can erase this particular difference invariant. Even if the invariant were present, it would not alone identify a decryption key.

## Reproduce

Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/run.py --check` and `python experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/check.py` from the repository root with NumPy installed. The [independent checker](experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/check.py) rebuilds all five partitions from Liberpedia's page transcriptions and counts the difference collisions with a separate pure-Python method. It also encrypts a planted three-unit example in both additive and Beaufort forms and verifies that each unit's shift cancels.

For the full upstream Monte Carlo replay, clone the [pinned source repository](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus), check out `bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c`, install NumPy, and run `python experiments/records/wulfic-stage-af-unit-shifts/replay_source.py --source-dir PATH_TO_CLONE`. The wrapper hashes source code and inputs, runs in a temporary output directory, and compares both resulting tables byte-for-byte.

records.title: Prime-indexed-prime and P.S. keys with a corrected IoC screen
records.question: When the archived program’s unreachable raw-IoC gate is explicitly corrected to 29×raw IoC >1.3, what do its called PIP and P.S. key grids yield on their verified page inputs?
records.summary: The source gate raw IoC >1.3 is impossible. Under a separately frozen normalized-IoC amendment, the complete 102,036-setting source grid produces no score over 1.3; 157 of 199 full-search shuffles reach at least the observed maximum.

record_type.label: Bounded solving test
record_type.description: Applies a fixed decoding, extraction or payload-retrieval rule to declared unsolved material, or excludes a specific direct-generation rule. Its result covers only those bounds.

scope.representation: Pinned Wulfic source page_21–54 flat GP29 rune streams and separator-defined word lengths, verified equal to the corresponding LP2-04–37 site records.
scope.procedure: Generate the source PIP stream and three P.S.-number encodings, apply all eligible source offsets and three decode directions, require all one-rune words to be I/A, then screen by 29×raw IoC >1.3. Repeat the complete selected-max search on 199 page shuffles.
scope.parameters: Million-limit source sieve; PIP n bound 50,000 and offsets 0–999; P.S. digit/pair/base29 encodings and offsets 0–49 subject to source length check; sub/add/Beaufort. Source page ordinals 21–54 map to LP2-04–37. No 7×7 key execution.
scope.exclusions: The original impossible raw-IoC hit gate is an audit, not a negative cipher test. No new key schedule, padding, cycling, altered singleton rule, replacement English scorer, other page range or claim of plaintext.

records.finding: After the corrected score gate, 3,031 settings pass the source singleton filter and none exceeds 1.3. The global maximum is 1.226492057 on LP2-14. In 157/199 whole-search page shuffles, the maximum is at least as large. The two short P.S. encodings have no eligible page length and the digit encoding has no singleton-admissible setting.
records.limitations: This concerns one explicitly amended score screen and the finite called source grids. The shuffle distribution is a selection control rather than a cipher model, and neither the original zero-hit output nor this corrected variant excludes PIP/P.S. keys under other rules.

# Prime-indexed-prime and P.S. keys under a corrected score

An [archived structural-analysis script](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/structural_analysis.py) tries a stream of **prime-indexed primes** and three numerical encodings of its **P.S. number** as rune keys. Its original hit rule requires a raw coincidence score above **1.3**, although that score cannot exceed **1**. The source's absence of hits therefore says nothing about its keys. We tested a clearly labeled amendment: multiply that score by **29** before applying the source's 1.3 screen, leaving its called key generators, page range, offsets, three directions and one-rune-word check intact.

![The impossible source score gate, corrected maximum, and whole-search shuffle comparison.](experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/comparison.svg)

**The corrected search has no screen hit.** Its highest score is **1.226** on LP2-14, below 1.3. In **157 of 199** page-shuffled whole searches, the best score was at least as high as the manuscript maximum; **27** shuffled searches even crossed 1.3. That comparison includes the same choice across pages, keys, offsets and directions. It is a selection control, not a cipher model; neither a low score nor a threshold crossing would itself identify a reading.

## What was searched

The source's `page_21` through `page_54` now correspond to **LP2-04 through LP2-37**. Their flat rune sequences and source-style word boundaries match the pinned source files. The search covers **102,036 settings**: 34 pages × 1,000 prime-indexed-prime offsets × three directions, plus 36 eligible P.S. **decimal-digit** settings. The source's digit-pair and base-29 keys have 66 and 90 symbols; every target page is at least 121 runes long, so neither has an eligible source-defined offset. We did not pad or repeat them. The source prints a partial 7×7 square but never searches it; it is outside this record.

For each setting we apply subtraction, addition or Beaufort decoding modulo 29. Before scoring, every visible one-rune word must decode to the GP indices for **I** or **A**. Only **3,031** of the 102,036 settings pass that filter on the actual pages; all are from the prime stream. The score is `29 × Σ f(f−1) / [n(n−1)]`, where `f` counts each decoded rune and `n` is the page's rune count. The highest-scoring page, LP2-14, has **no one-rune words**, so its 3,000 prime-stream settings all pass that particular filter. No P.S. candidate passes it on the two eligible pages.

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/plan.json) fixes this amended rule and 199 full-search shuffles before the manuscript scan. The [input audit](experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/input-audit.json) records source and local hashes and exact word lengths for all 34 pages. A [source parity check](experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/source-parity.json) compared the GP map, million-limit prime sieve, four derived key streams, decode directions, singleton rule and coincidence arithmetic with the exact pinned program. Twelve planted cases—each key stream in all three directions—recover complete known text and clear the amended screen. These controls show that the corrected screen can report a genuine keyed message; they do not validate an LP2 reading.

## Reproduce

From the checkout or [experiment ZIP](downloads/experiments/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized.zip), run from its root:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/run.py --gate --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/run.py --run --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/check.py
python experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/plot.py --check
```

The [results](experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/results.json) retain the page maxima and every shuffle maximum; the independent checker reruns the full source-defined grid and all 199 controls with a separate sieve and scorer. To repeat the optional direct source-function comparison, download the exact pinned source file linked above and run `python experiments/records/wulfic-structural-pip-ps-normalized/source_parity.py --source PATH --check` from the bundle root. The original raw-score gate remains impossible; this result belongs only to the explicitly corrected variant and the source's finite inputs.

records.title: Prime streams and a short feedback key
records.question: Do the exact executed prime-derived and two-value feedback searches in archived stream_cipher_attack.py provide a distinctive LP2 reading under the source's own score?
records.summary: The full pinned source searches produce many threshold hits, but complete searches on 19 shuffled versions do too. The score does not establish a reading.

record_type.label: Method replay
record_type.description: Reconstructs a supplied proposed method and its choices; reproduction is not independent confirmation of a reading.

scope.representation: Pinned source Git-object rune text using its exact GP29 alphabet and period/hyphen/bullet/space/newline word separators. Source page_18..55 maps to current LP2-01..38; separate LFSR selection is LP2-28,10,17.
scope.procedure: Run every entry of the source's 26-stream dictionary in three modes over every eligible source page. Run all 29^4 ordered two-value LFSR state/tap tuples in three modes over the three highest-singleton pages, including zero/singular tap cases. Preserve the source IoC, bigram and I/A singleton score and hit thresholds. Repeat the entire selected grids on 19 within-page rune shuffles.
scope.parameters: 2,964 stream page-settings; 6,365,529 LFSR page-settings; source thresholds combined>2 or IoC>1.5 for streams, combined>3 for LFSR; shuffle seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Uncalled Fibonacci generator, incomplete Berlekamp–Massey key reconstruction, pages outside source selection, other prime rules, longer/nonlinear feedback or different alphabet/language models.

records.finding: On 38 matched LP2 pages, 2,964 prime-stream settings yielded 644 source-threshold hits (19 shuffled-search range 625–702). On three selected pages, all 6,365,529 two-value LFSR settings yielded 38,826 hits (shuffled range 33,694–44,833). The best stream IoC 1.140 was reached or exceeded by 16/19 controls; the best LFSR combined score was reached or exceeded by 11/19.
records.limitations: The source's IoC/bigram/I-or-A-singleton score is a permissive candidate screen, not a reading test. Nineteen within-page shuffles supply only a coarse descriptive selection control and are not a cipher model. Old source page labels actually select LP2-01–38; the source-defined but uncalled Fibonacci stream and unfinished Berlekamp–Massey reconstruction are excluded. Other generator lengths, feedback clocks and page ranges remain open.

# Prime streams and a short feedback key

An [archived solver script](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/blob/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy/stream_cipher_attack.py) searches two ways of generating a rune-by-rune key: fixed sequences drawn from primes, and a key in which each new value depends on the previous two. We replayed its complete *executed* grids on the corresponding manuscript pages.

**The script's threshold admits many outputs, but does not identify a reading.** On rune-shuffled versions of the same pages, complete searches also find thousands of hits. The observed best scores sit within the ranges of 19 shuffled searches. These controls show why crossing the source threshold is insufficient; shuffling is not a model of every possible cipher.

![Source-threshold hit counts in the manuscript compared with complete searches on 19 shuffled versions](experiments/records/wulfic-systematic-stream-source/comparison.svg)

| Source branch | Exact search | Manuscript threshold hits | Nineteen complete shuffled searches |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prime-derived streams | 2,964 settings on 38 pages | 644 | 625–702 hits; median 662 |
| Two-value LFSR | 6,365,529 settings on 3 pages | 38,826 | 33,694–44,833 hits; median 38,452 |

The stream branch's highest index of coincidence is **1.140**, exceeded by **16 of 19** shuffled searches. Its best combined score is exceeded by **5 of 19**. The LFSR branch's best combined score is exceeded by **11 of 19**. Nineteen controls give a coarse comparison, not a precise probability. There is no independently predicted longer passage or untouched page in the source rule.

The script calls its target list “all unsolved pages,” but its old folder names resolve differently. After its exclusions and empty-page checks, it actually reads archived `page_18` through `page_55`, corresponding to **LP2-01–38**. The two older files `page_00` and `page_02` contain no runes. The source then selects the three pages with the most visible one-rune words for the LFSR search: **LP2-28, LP2-10 and LP2-17**. Of these, LP2-28 overlaps the earlier [singleton-LFSR test](#/experiments/wulfic-lfsr-singleton-constraints), which used a different constraint solver and page set.

## What the screens measure

The script tries **26 named prime-derived streams** in subtraction, addition and Beaufort directions. They include prime values, prime minus one, prime gaps and two cumulative sequences. Each begins at page position zero. The separate feedback search tries every initial pair and coefficient pair modulo 29: **29⁴** tuples on each of three pages, again in three directions. Zero coefficients and degenerate sequences are included. These parameter combinations are settings inside two method branches, not millions of independent ideas.

Each decoded output receives an index of coincidence, a count of ten favored rune pairs, and credit when a visible one-rune word becomes **I** or **A**. That last component can dominate: on LP2-38, where the source parser finds only one one-rune word, matching it adds **five points** to a stream score whose hit threshold is two. The best LFSR setting on LP2-17 makes **6 of 10** one-rune words I or A; its index of coincidence is **0.976**. A partial crib fit and a selected score are not a sentence.

The source defines a Fibonacci-prime generator but never adds it to the search table. Its later Berlekamp–Massey section has a `pass` where a full key would be reconstructed. Neither is counted here as an executed decoder. Other prime streams and other feedback lengths remain outside this test.

## How the replay was checked

Before scoring manuscript text, all 26 generators matched the pinned source functions at four lengths. A sample of 107 feedback tuples, including zero states and taps, matched the source's key, decoded runes, and complete score in all three directions. A synthetic known plaintext recovered exactly and passed each source screen. The optimized search then tested every declared setting. An independent scalar checker recalculates all retained winners and their full-decoding hashes and repeats one entire shuffled feedback search.

The [frozen plan](experiments/records/wulfic-systematic-stream-source/plan.json), [pinned input snapshot](experiments/records/wulfic-systematic-stream-source/inputs.json), and [results](experiments/records/wulfic-systematic-stream-source/results.json) give the exact bounds and counts. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-systematic-stream-source/check.py` to check the saved result. Run `python experiments/records/wulfic-systematic-stream-source/run.py --check` to repeat all grids and controls; this requires Python, NumPy and Numba. With a checkout of the pinned source revision, `gate.py --source-root PATH --check` and `snapshot_inputs.py --source-root PATH --check` verify source parity and original inputs.

The historical outputs in the archived repository are not treated as verified. This is a corrected-input replay of its finite callable branches, not an exclusion of prime-based keys or LFSRs generally.

records.title: Do the proposed two-time-pad regions match?
records.question: Do the six fixed aligned-copy regions in three pinned Wulfic legacy scripts exist on their verified LP2 input, and what does the separate page-pair difference screen show?
records.summary: The three scripts’ specific identical-span premises fail on their committed source pages; a separate page-pair frequency screen does not establish key reuse.

record_type.label: Method replay
record_type.description: Reconstructs a supplied proposed method and its choices; reproduction is not independent confirmation of a reading.

scope.representation: Corrected source old page_21–54 = LP2-04–37, GP29 rune-only, continuous 8,226-rune stream. Label-disambiguation check on LP2-27 and LP2-44. Four direct-reading LP1 pages provide matched-length planted pairs.
scope.procedure: Check all six source asserted identical regions, the claimed page27/page44 prefix and period bounds on the original committed Git page objects; replay the separate all-page-pair ±IoC source function, then 199 whole-search page-wise shuffles and all ten fixed 137-rune shared-key plants.
scope.parameters: Six asserted regions, one 6,726-rune period, 34 pages, 561 unordered pairs ×2 operations=1,122 screens, IoC>1.15, 199 seeded full-search shuffles (seed20261023), five 137-rune reading windows forming ten fixed pairs.
scope.exclusions: Unknown key-reuse alignments or periods, arbitrary key clocks, crib readability scoring under the failed source-copy assumption, alternative transcriptions, and separate solved/reference-text running-key branches.

records.finding: The corrected source stream has 8,226 runes. Five of six proposed paired regions exceed it; the sole in-bounds region matches at 7/404 aligned positions and differs at the first. The P27/P44 prefix also fails. The independent 1,122-case page-pair screen reaches IoC 1.2296 at most; 43/199 page-shuffled full searches reach at least that maximum. Only 2/10 matched-length planted known-reading pairs encrypted with a shared key cross the source 1.15 threshold.
records.limitations: This falsifies six named identical-ciphertext premises, not general shared-key encryption: equal keys can yield different ciphertexts when plaintexts differ, and equal ciphertext alone does not prove equal keys. All 34 source page blobs exist in Git despite the sparse local checkout and match the site pages; the source pair-score functions were replayed exactly. The period and crib loops based on the failed alignments are not meaningful complete decoding tests. The page-pair controls were added after preliminary outcomes were viewed. Page shuffling preserves unigram counts, not natural plaintext, and the IoC screen misses most planted reuse pairs at length 137. Running-key branches of one source script are separate from this grouped claim.
records.article:
# Do the proposed two-time-pad regions actually match?

Three [archived Wulfic scripts](https://github.com/Wulfic/Cicada3301-Liber_Primus/tree/bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c/tools/legacy) propose paired rune positions where a key could be reused. Their crib-dragging rules depend on those positions lining up. **The six claimed copies do not match the verified manuscript text.** Five point past the end of the scripts' own page stream. The one pair entirely inside that stream has only **7 equal runes in 404 aligned positions**, with a mismatch at the first position.

This checks the scripts' **specific claim of identical ciphertext spans**. Sharing an additive key does *not* require identical ciphertext: if the plaintexts differ, their ciphertexts normally differ too. Conversely, identical ciphertext alone would not prove that the keys match. The failed copy claim cannot support these crib placements, but it does not settle the general key-reuse question.

![Five proposed paired regions exceed the source stream; the in-bounds pair has 7 equal runes out of 404. A separate pairwise statistic is close to its shuffled-search median.](experiments/records/wulfic-two-time-pad-premise/alignment.svg)

The source calls its input files pages 21–54. We recovered **all 34 page files from the pinned source commit's Git objects**; their rune contents match the [verified input mapping](experiments/records/wulfic-keyword-prime-layer-grid/source-gp-hashes.json) to **LP2-04–37**, an **8,226-rune** stream. The files were merely omitted from the sparse local checkout. The proposed period of 6,726 would require positions through 13,451 for its first two blocks. Its subtraction loop cannot run on this input. The other script says its page 27 is a prefix of page 44. On the correctly mapped pages, those are LP2-10 and LP2-27: only **9 of the 234 available aligned runes** agree, beginning with a mismatch. Reading the labels instead as LP2-27 and LP2-44 still does not rescue the claim: **13 of 234** agree, again with a mismatch at the start.

One script also makes a separate, finite measurement: subtract or add every pair among those 34 pages, align at page starts, and screen the resulting rune frequencies. We replayed all **1,122** page-pair/operation cases and confirmed each score against the pinned script's own functions and committed page files. Five crossed its IoC screen of 1.15; the highest is **1.23** for LP2-12 against LP2-14 over **137 runes**. This is a selected frequency score, not readable plaintext. In a retrospective control that shuffles each page once per trial and repeats the whole pair search, **43 of 199** trials reached at least 1.23. The shuffled-search median was **1.19**.

The source screen has limited power at those lengths. When we encrypted ten fixed pairs of established LP1 readings with a deliberately shared key, only **two of ten** differences crossed 1.15. A score below that line therefore cannot rule out every reused key. The shuffles preserve each page's rune counts; they show how the *maximum of this search* behaves under that conditional comparison, not the chance that an arbitrary cipher is correct.

This result rejects the **specific claimed aligned-copy regions** as a basis for these crib placements. It does not exclude other two-time-pad or key-reuse models, which could use different ciphertexts and still share a key. We did not score cribs under a shared-key assumption whose named alignments fail the input check. The source script's running-key branches are separate proposals; [solved-text running keys](#/experiments/solved-reading-running-key) and [an Emerson running key](#/experiments/emerson-running-key) have their own bounded records.

The [plan](experiments/records/wulfic-two-time-pad-premise/plan.json) pins the three source files, exact page mapping, six paired spans, pairwise screen and controls. It is a **retrospective replay plan**: preliminary page results were inspected before the local plan was written, and the 199 shuffles are a diagnostic rather than a prospective discovery test. [Results](experiments/records/wulfic-two-time-pad-premise/results.json) retain every proposed region, the five threshold hits, all control maxima and all ten planted pairs.

To reproduce from a full Liberpedia checkout, run:

```text
python experiments/records/wulfic-two-time-pad-premise/run.py --check
python experiments/records/wulfic-two-time-pad-premise/check.py
python experiments/records/wulfic-two-time-pad-premise/plot.py --check
```

The independent checker reads the page JSON separately from the producer's text files. Pass `--source-root PATH_TO_WULFIC_CHECKOUT` to the checker to verify the three original script hashes, all 34 page Git objects and every page-pair score from the source functions at commit `bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c`. A sparse checkout works if those Git objects are present.
